title.zh: 卷二百四十七 列傳第六 宗室四
title.raw: 卷二百四十七 列傳第六 宗室四 Volume 247 Biographies 6: Imperial Clan 4

sentences.zh: 子淔字正之，燕王五世孫。

translations.literal: Zizi, courtesy name Zhengzhi, was a fifth-generation descendant of the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zizi (Zhengzhi) was a fifth-generation descendant of the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 父令鑠，官至寶文閣待制。

translations.literal: His father Ling Yue reached the office of Attendant Gentleman of the Baowen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ling Yue had risen to Attendant Gentleman of the Baowen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 子淔以蔭補承務郎，累遷少府監主簿，改河南少尹。

translations.literal: Zizi entered service by hereditary privilege as Gentleman for Court Service, was promoted in succession to Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Manufactories, and was reassigned as Vice Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zizi entered office through hereditary privilege as Gentleman for Court Service, rose through successive posts to Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Manufactories, and was then appointed Vice Administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時治西內，子淔有幹才，漕使宋昪器之。

translations.literal: At the time the Western Inner Palace was under construction; Zizi had administrative talent, and the transport commissioner Song Bian valued him.
translations.idiomatic: While the Western Inner Palace was being built, Zizi proved himself capable, and Transport Commissioner Song Bian took a strong liking to him.

sentences.zh: 或事有未便，子淔輒力爭，昪每改容謝之。

translations.literal: Whenever some matter was ill-advised, Zizi would argue forcefully, and Bian would each time change his expression and apologize to him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a plan seemed ill-advised, Zizi would argue it out firmly, and Bian would each time soften his manner and yield.

sentences.zh: 除蔡河撥發綱運官。

translations.literal: He was appointed officer for dispatching transport convoys on the Cai River.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to oversee convoy dispatch on the Cai River.

sentences.zh: 會夏旱，河水涸，轉餉後期，貶秩一級。

translations.literal: It happened that a summer drought dried up the river; grain transport fell behind schedule, and he was demoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: A summer drought left the river dry, grain shipments fell behind schedule, and he was demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 提舉三門、白波輦運事，除直秘閣。

translations.literal: He was put in charge of transport affairs at Sanmen and Baibo, and was appointed Direct Attendant of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed in charge of transport at Sanmen and Baibo and appointed Direct Attendant of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，起復。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother, then was recalled to office before the mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he entered mourning, but was soon recalled to duty.

sentences.zh: 累進龍圖閣、秘閣修撰，除陝西轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Compiler of the Dragon Diagram Hall and the Secret Archive, and was appointed Vice Commissioner of Transport for Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Compiler of the Dragon Diagram Hall and the Secret Archive, then was appointed Vice Commissioner of Transport for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初，蔡京鑄夾錫錢，民病壅滯，子淔請鑄小鐵錢以權之，因範格以進。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cai Jing had cast tin-plated coins; the people suffered from blockage in circulation. Zizi requested casting small iron coins as a counterweight, and submitted a model specification.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cai Jing had introduced tin-plated coins, and the people suffered from clogged circulation. Zizi proposed casting small iron coins to balance them and submitted a model for approval.

sentences.zh: 徽宗大說，御書「宣和通寶」四字爲錢文。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong was greatly pleased and personally wrote the four characters "Xuanhe Tongbao" as the coin inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong was delighted and personally wrote the four characters "Xuanhe Tongbao" for the coin legend.

sentences.zh: 既成，子淔奏令民以舊銅錢入官，易新鐵錢。

translations.literal: When they were finished, Zizi memorialized that the people should turn in old copper coins to the government and exchange them for new iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: Once the new coins were ready, Zizi proposed that the people surrender old copper cash to the government in exchange for the new iron currency.

sentences.zh: 旬日，易得百餘萬緡。

translations.literal: Within ten days, more than a million strings were easily obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the exchange had easily brought in more than a million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 帝手劄以新錢百萬緡付五路，均糴細麥，命子淔領其事。

translations.literal: The emperor by autograph note assigned a million strings of the new money to the five circuits for equalized purchase of fine wheat, and ordered Zizi to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor by personal note allocated a million strings of the new coins to the five circuits to buy fine wheat on equal terms, and put Zizi in charge.

sentences.zh: 民苦限迫，詣子淔訴者日數百人，子淔奏請寬其期，民便之。

translations.literal: The people suffered under the tight deadline; several hundred a day came to Zizi to plead. Zizi memorialized to extend the period, to the people's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The people buckled under the tight deadline, and hundreds came to Zizi each day to plead. He memorialized for an extension, which greatly relieved them.

sentences.zh: 會蔡京再相，言者希京意，論子淔亂錢法，落職奉祠。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing became chief minister again, critics currying favor with Jing accused Zizi of disrupting the currency system; he was removed from office and given a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing returned as chief minister, critics eager to please him charged Zizi with wrecking the currency system, and he was stripped of office and given a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，復秘閣修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, he was restored as Compiler of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang era he was restored as Compiler of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 金人侵洛，子淔奔荊南。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded Luoyang, Zizi fled to Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens invaded Luoyang, Zizi fled south to Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 潰兵祝靖、盛德破荊南城，子淔匿民家，靖等知之，來謁，言京城已破。

translations.literal: Routed troops Zhu Jing and Sheng De stormed Jingnan city. Zizi hid in a commoner's house; Jing and the others learned of it, came to call on him, and said the capital had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Routed soldiers Zhu Jing and Sheng De overran Jingnan. Zizi hid in a private home, but they found him, came to pay their respects, and told him the capital had fallen.

sentences.zh: 子淔泣，說之曰「君輩宜亟還都城，護社稷，取功名，無貪財擾州縣也。」

translations.literal: Zizi wept and admonished them, saying, "You gentlemen should hurry back to the capital, guard the altars of state, win merit and fame, and not plunder wealth and harass the prefectures and counties."
translations.idiomatic: Zizi wept and urged them: "You should hurry back to the capital, defend the realm, win honor in battle, and not loot the countryside or harass the districts."

sentences.zh: 皆應曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: They all answered, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "We will."

sentences.zh: 子淔因草檄趣之。

translations.literal: Zizi then drafted a proclamation to urge them on.
translations.idiomatic: Zizi then drafted a proclamation to hurry them north.

sentences.zh: 翌日，靖等遂北行。

translations.literal: The next day, Jing and the others set out north.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jing and his men marched north.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，召見，復徽猷閣直學士、知西外宗正司，改江西都轉運使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing he was summoned to audience, restored as Direct Academician of the Huixian Pavilion and Administrator of the Western Outer Imperial Clan Office, and transferred to Commissioner of Transport for all of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 1 he was summoned to court, restored as Direct Academician of the Huixian Pavilion and put in charge of the Western Outer Imperial Clan Office, then made Commissioner of Transport for all Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 時建督府，軍須浩繁，子淔運餉不絕，以功進寶文閣直學士，再知西外宗正司。

translations.literal: At the time a supervisory headquarters was being established and military supplies were vast; Zizi kept grain transport unbroken, and for this merit was promoted to Direct Academician of the Baowen Pavilion and again made Administrator of the Western Outer Imperial Clan Office.
translations.idiomatic: A supervisory headquarters had been set up and military needs were enormous; Zizi kept supplies flowing without interruption, and for this was promoted to Direct Academician of the Baowen Pavilion and again put in charge of the Western Outer Imperial Clan Office.

sentences.zh: 三京新復，除京畿都轉運使，以疾辭。

translations.literal: When the three capitals were newly recovered, he was appointed Commissioner of Transport for the Capital Region, but resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the three capitals were newly recovered he was appointed Commissioner of Transport for the Capital Region, but declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，年六十七。

translations.literal: He died at home, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子淔幼警悟，蘇軾過其家，抱置膝上，謂其父曰：「此公家千里駒也。」

translations.literal: Zizi was clever and quick as a child. When Su Shi visited his home, he took him on his knee and said to his father, "This is a thousand-li steed of your house."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zizi was unusually bright. Su Shi once visited the family, lifted him onto his knee, and told his father, "This child is a thoroughbred of your clan."

sentences.zh: 及長，善談論，工詩。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was skilled in discourse and accomplished in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he was an engaging talker and a capable poet.

sentences.zh: 然崇甯、大觀間土木繁興，子淔每董其役，識者鄙之。

translations.literal: Yet during the Chongning and Daguan reigns, when construction projects flourished, Zizi often supervised the labor, and men of judgment looked down on him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet during the Chongning and Daguan reigns, when building projects multiplied, Zizi often directed the work himself, and thoughtful observers held him in low regard for it.

sentences.zh: 子崧字伯山，燕懿王後五世孫。

translations.literal: Zisong, courtesy name Boshan, was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Yi of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zisong (Boshan) was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Yi of Yan.

sentences.zh: 登崇甯五年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Chongning 5.

sentences.zh: 宣和間，官至宗正少卿，除徽猷閣直學士、知淮寧府。

translations.literal: During the Xuanhe reign he reached Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and was appointed Direct Academician of the Huixian Pavilion and Prefect of Huaining.
translations.idiomatic: During Xuanhe he rose to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, then was made Direct Academician of the Huixian Pavilion and Prefect of Huaining.

sentences.zh: 汴京失守，起兵勤王，道阻未得進。

translations.literal: When Bianjing fell, he raised troops to rescue the throne, but the roads were blocked and he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Bianjing fell he raised troops to rescue the throne, but the roads were blocked and he could not get through.

sentences.zh: 聞張邦昌僭位，以書白康王：宜遣師邀金人河上，迎請兩宮，問罪僭逆，若議渡江，恐誤大計。

translations.literal: Hearing that Zhang Bangchang had usurped the throne, he wrote to Prince Kang: troops should be sent to intercept the Jurchens on the river, to welcome back the two palaces and punish the usurper; if the plan were to cross the Yangzi, he feared the great strategy would be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Zhang Bangchang had seized the throne, he wrote to Prince Kang urging him to send troops to block the Jurchens on the Yellow River, bring back the two sovereigns, and punish the usurper, warning that any plan to retreat south across the Yangzi would ruin the larger strategy.

sentences.zh: 遂與知潁昌府何志同等盟，傳檄中外。

translations.literal: He then joined in alliance with He Zhigong, Prefect of Yingchang, and circulated proclamations within and beyond the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then allied with He Zhigong, Prefect of Yingchang, and issued proclamations throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 已而聞金人退，引兵襄邑，遣范塤、徐文中詣濟州，請王進兵南京，且言：「國家之制，無視王在外者，主上特付大王以元帥之權，此殆天意。

translations.literal: Later, hearing the Jurchens had withdrawn, he led his troops to Xiangyi and sent Fan Kun and Xu Wenzhong to Jizhou to ask the prince to advance on the Southern Capital, saying: "By the institutions of the state, no prince outside the capital is overlooked; the sovereign has specially entrusted Your Highness with the authority of commander-in-chief—this is surely Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the Jurchens had withdrawn, he marched to Xiangyi and sent Fan Kun and Xu Wenzhong to Jizhou to urge the prince to advance on the Southern Capital, writing: "By our laws no prince abroad is left out of account; the throne has given you full command—surely this is Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 亟宜承制號召四方豪傑，則中原可傳檄而定。」

translations.literal: You should promptly assume imperial authority and summon heroes from all quarters; then the Central Plain can be settled by proclamation alone."
translations.idiomatic: You should act at once under imperial mandate and rally heroes from every quarter; the Central Plain could then be won by proclamation alone."

sentences.zh: 王命子崧充大元帥府參議官、東南道都總管。

translations.literal: The prince appointed Zisong Counselor of the Grand Marshal's Headquarters and Overall Commander of the Southeast Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The prince made Zisong Counselor of the Grand Marshal's Headquarters and Overall Commander of the Southeast Circuit.

sentences.zh: 邦昌家在廬州，子崧檄通守趙令儦幾察之，且請捕誅其母子，以絕奸心。

translations.literal: Bangchang's family was in Luzhou. Zisong sent a dispatch to the transit intendant Zhao Lingyi to keep close watch, and also requested that mother and son be seized and executed to cut off treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang's family was in Luzhou. Zisong ordered Transit Intendant Zhao Lingyi to keep them under close surveillance and asked that mother and son be arrested and executed to forestall any treachery.

sentences.zh: 又言：「自圍城以來，朝命隔絕，乞下諸路，凡有事宜，並取大元帥府裁決，偽檄毋輒行。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since the siege, court orders have been cut off. I beg that all circuits be instructed that every matter is to be decided by the Grand Marshal's Headquarters, and that forged proclamations must not be circulated at will.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged: "Since the siege court orders have not reached the provinces. Order every circuit to refer all affairs to the Grand Marshal's Headquarters and not to act on forged proclamations.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使范訥逗撓營私，所宜加罪。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Fan Ne has dallied and pursued private gain; he should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Fan Ne has dragged his feet and pursued private gain; he deserves punishment.

sentences.zh: 宜蠲被兵州縣租，經理淮南、荊、浙形勢之地，毋爲群盜所據。」

translations.literal: Rent in prefectures and counties ravaged by war should be remitted, and the strategic positions in Huainan, Jing, and Zhe should be secured so that they are not seized by bandit gangs."
translations.idiomatic: Remit taxes in war-torn districts, secure the strategic points in Huainan, Jing, and Zhe, and keep them from falling to bandit armies."

sentences.zh: 檄止諸路毋受邦昌偽赦，移書責邦昌曰：「人臣當見危致命，今議者籍籍，謂劫請傾危之計實由閣下，不然，金人何堅拒孫傅之請，而卒歸于閣下也。

translations.literal: He issued proclamations forbidding the circuits to accept Bangchang's false amnesty, and sent a letter rebuking Bangchang: "A minister should face peril and give his life. Talk is rife that the scheme of coerced enthronement that endangered the state came from Your Lordship; otherwise why did the Jurchens firmly reject Sun Fu's plea yet in the end enthrone Your Lordship?
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the circuits not to accept Bangchang's false amnesty and wrote to rebuke him: "A loyal minister dies when the state is in peril. Rumor everywhere says the plot to force a puppet throne was yours; otherwise why did the Jurchens reject Sun Fu's pleas yet put you on the throne in the end?

sentences.zh: 敵既遠去，宜速反正，若少遲疑，則天下共誅逆節，雖悔無及矣。」

translations.literal: The enemy has already withdrawn far away; you should quickly restore the rightful order. If you hesitate even slightly, the whole realm will join in punishing your treason, and regret will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy has withdrawn; restore the legitimate order at once. Hesitate, and the whole empire will rise to punish your treason—then regret will be useless."

sentences.zh: 又遺書王時雍曰：「諸公相與亡人之國，方且以爲佐命功臣，不知平日所學何事。」

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Wang Shiyong saying: "You gentlemen together destroyed another man's state, yet now take yourselves for founding ministers—one wonders what you studied in ordinary times."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Wang Shiyong: "You have together ruined a dynasty, yet fancy yourselves founding ministers—what, one wonders, did you ever learn?"

sentences.zh: 會邦昌遣使迎王次第白子崧，子崧即貽王書曰：「似聞謂以京師殘破，不可復入，止欲即位軍中，便圖遷徙，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: When Bangchang sent envoys to welcome the prince, they informed Zisong in turn. Zisong at once wrote to the prince: "I seem to hear it said that because the capital lies in ruins it cannot be re-entered, and that Your Highness intends only to take the throne in camp and then plan relocation—I am privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: When Bangchang's envoys came to welcome the prince they told Zisong as much, and he at once wrote to the prince: "I hear that because the capital is in ruins you mean to be enthroned only in camp and then move south—I cannot make sense of this.

sentences.zh: 夫欲致中興，當謹舉措，宜先謁宗廟，覲母后，明正誅賞，降霈四方。

translations.literal: If one wishes to bring about restoration, one must act with care: first visit the ancestral temples, pay court to the empress dowager, clarify rewards and punishments, and extend grace to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: To restore the dynasty you must act with care: first visit the ancestral shrines, pay homage to the empress dowager, make rewards and punishments clear, and extend grace throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 若京師果不可都，然後徐議所向。」

translations.literal: Only if the capital truly cannot serve as seat of government should one then slowly discuss where to go."
translations.idiomatic: Only if the capital truly cannot be restored as seat of government should you then, and slowly, decide where to go."

sentences.zh: 遂傳檄京師，奏于隆祐太后曰：「諸路先聞二聖北遷，易姓改國，恐間有假討逆之名，以竊據州郡者。

translations.literal: He then circulated proclamations in the capital and memorialized Empress Dowager Longyou: "The circuits have already heard that the two sovereigns were taken north and the dynasty changed its name; I fear that here and there men may borrow the name of punishing rebellion to seize prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued proclamations in the capital and memorialized Empress Dowager Longyou: "The provinces have heard that both sovereigns were taken north and the dynasty usurped; I fear some may use the pretense of punishing rebels to seize districts for themselves.

sentences.zh: 乞速下明詔，諭四方以迎立康王之意，庶幾人心慰安，奸宄自消矣。」

translations.literal: I beg that a clear edict be issued at once, informing the four quarters of the intent to welcome Prince Kang to the throne, so that hearts may be reassured and traitors may disappear of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Issue a clear edict at once telling the empire that Prince Kang is to be enthroned, so that hearts may be steadied and traitors may melt away."

sentences.zh: 尋以所部兵會濟州。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he joined the prince at Jizhou with his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he brought his troops to join the prince at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 康王即位，子崧請放諸路常平積欠錢，又言：「台諫爲人主耳目，近年用非其人，率取旨言事。

translations.literal: When Prince Kang took the throne, Zisong requested remission of accumulated arrears in the Ever-Normal granary funds in all circuits, and also said: "The censorate and remonstrance bureau are the ruler's eyes and ears; in recent years unfit men have been appointed, who generally take their cue from the throne in speaking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kang was enthroned, Zisong asked that accumulated Ever-Normal granary debts in every circuit be forgiven, and said: "The censorate and remonstrance bureau are the ruler's eyes and ears, yet lately unworthy men have been appointed who merely echo the throne.

sentences.zh: 請尊舊制，聽學士、中丞互舉。

translations.literal: I ask that the old system be honored, allowing academicians and vice censors to nominate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the old practice and let academicians and vice censors nominate one another.

sentences.zh: 范祖禹、常安民、上官均先朝言事盡忠，請錄其子。」

translations.literal: Fan Zuyu, Chang Anmin, and Shangguan Jun of the previous reign spoke on affairs with full loyalty; I ask that their sons be enrolled in office."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zuyu, Chang Anmin, and Shangguan Jun served the previous reign with loyal remonstrance; enroll their sons in office."

sentences.zh: 帝皆可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all his memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 因建三屯之議：一屯澶淵，一屯河中、陝、華，一屯青、鄆間，以張聲勢。

translations.literal: He then proposed the plan of three garrisons: one at Chanyuan, one in the Hezhong, Shaan, and Hua region, and one between Qing and Yan, to display military strength.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed three garrisons—at Chanyuan, in the Hezhong-Shaan-Hua region, and between Qing and Yan—to project military strength.

sentences.zh: 萬一敵騎南侵，則三道並進，可成大功。

translations.literal: If by chance enemy cavalry should invade south, the three routes could advance together and achieve a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy cavalry should strike south, the three columns could advance together and win a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 除延康殿學士、知鎮江府、兩浙路兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Yankang Hall, Prefect of Zhenjiang, and Military Controller of the Two Zhe Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Academician of the Yankang Hall, Prefect of Zhenjiang, and Military Controller of the Two Zhe Circuits.

sentences.zh: 上章論王時雍、徐秉哲、吳開、莫儔、范瓊、胡思、王紹、王及之、顏博文、余大均等逼遷上皇，取太子，辱六宮，捕宗室，竊禁物，都人指爲國賊。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing Wang Shiyong, Xu Bingzhe, Wu Kai, Mo Chou, Fan Qiong, Hu Si, Wang Shao, Wang Jizhi, Yan Bowen, Yu Dajun, and others for coercing the retired emperor's removal, seizing the crown prince, shaming the six palaces, arresting imperial clansmen, and stealing forbidden treasures—the capital's people pointed to them as traitors to the state.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized against Wang Shiyong, Xu Bingzhe, Wu Kai, Mo Chou, Fan Qiong, Hu Si, Wang Shao, Wang Jizhi, Yan Bowen, Yu Dajun, and others for forcing the retired emperor north, seizing the crown prince, shaming the palace women, arresting clansmen, and looting the imperial storehouses—men of the capital called them traitors.

sentences.zh: 伏望肆諸市朝，以爲臣子之戒。

translations.literal: I humbly hope they may be executed in the marketplace as a warning to ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that they be executed in public as a warning to every minister.

sentences.zh: 時滑州兩經殘破，子崧薦傅亮可任。

translations.literal: At the time Huazhou had twice been ravaged; Zisong recommended Fu Liang as fit for the post.
translations.idiomatic: Huazhou had twice been laid waste; Zisong recommended Fu Liang as capable of restoring it.

sentences.zh: 除亮滑州通判，黃潛善沮之，命遂寢。

translations.literal: Liang was appointed Vice Prefect of Huazhou, but Huang Qianshan obstructed it and the appointment was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was appointed Vice Prefect of Huazhou, but Huang Qianshan blocked the appointment and it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 賊趙萬犯鎮江，子崧遣將擊萬于丹徒，調鄉兵乘城爲備。

translations.literal: The bandit Zhao Wan attacked Zhenjiang. Zisong sent generals to strike Wan at Dantu and mobilized local militia to man the walls in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhao Wan attacked Zhenjiang. Zisong sent troops to fight him at Dantu and called up local militia to man the walls.

sentences.zh: 頃之，官軍敗歸，鄉兵驚潰，子崧率親兵保焦山寺，賊據鎮江。

translations.literal: Before long the government troops returned defeated; the militia panicked and scattered. Zisong led his personal guard to hold Jiaoshan Temple, and the bandits occupied Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the government troops retreated in defeat, the militia broke and fled, Zisong withdrew with his personal guard to Jiaoshan Temple, and the rebels seized Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 初，昌陵復土，司天監苗昌裔謂人曰：「太祖後當再有天下。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yongling Mausoleum was reburied, Astronomical Observer Miao Changyi of the Directorate of Astronomy said to people, "Descendants of Taizu will again possess the realm."
translations.idiomatic: When Yongling Mausoleum was reinterred, Astronomical Observer Miao Changyi of the Directorate of Astronomy told people, "Taizu's line will rule the realm again."

sentences.zh: 子崧習聞其說，靖康末起兵，檄文頗涉不遜。

translations.literal: Zisong had long been familiar with this saying; when he raised troops at the end of Jingkang, his proclamations were rather impertinent in tone.
translations.idiomatic: Zisong had long known this prophecy; when he raised troops at the end of Jingkang, his proclamations bordered on lèse-majesté.

sentences.zh: 子崧與御營統制辛道宗有隙，道示求得其文，上之。

translations.literal: Zisong had a feud with Xing Daozong, Commander of the Imperial Camp. Daozong sought and obtained his documents and presented them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zisong was at odds with Imperial Camp Commander Xing Daozong, who obtained his proclamations and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔年史往案其獄，情得，帝震怒，不欲暴其罪，坐以前擅棄城，降單州團練副使，謫居南雄州。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Nian Shi to investigate the case; the facts were established. The emperor was greatly angered but did not wish to expose the full crime; on the charge of earlier abandoning the city without authorization, Zisong was demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Danzhou and exiled to Nanxiong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Nian Shi to investigate; the facts were proved. The emperor was furious but did not wish to publicize the full charge; citing his earlier unauthorized abandonment of the city, he was demoted to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Danzhou and exiled to Nanxiong.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年赦，復集英殿修撰，而子崧已卒于貶所。

translations.literal: In the amnesty of the second year of Shaoxing he was restored as Compiler of the Hall for Gathering Excellence, but Zisong had already died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty of Shaoxing 2 restored him as Compiler of the Hall for Gathering Excellence, but Zisong had already died in exile.

sentences.zh: 子櫟，燕懿王後五世孫。

translations.literal: Zili was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Yi of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zili was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Yi of Yan.

sentences.zh: 登元祐六年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Yuanyou 6.

sentences.zh: 靖康中，爲汝州太守。

translations.literal: During Jingkang he was Grand Administrator of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang crisis he served as Grand Administrator of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 金人再渝盟，破荊湖諸州，獨子櫟能保境土。

translations.literal: The Jurchens broke the treaty again and overran the prefectures of Jing and Hu; only Zili was able to preserve his territory.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens broke the treaty again and overran Jing and Hu, only Zili held his territory intact.

sentences.zh: 李綱言于朝，遷寶文閣直學士，尋提舉萬壽觀。

translations.literal: Li Gang spoke of him at court; he was promoted to Direct Academician of the Baowen Pavilion and soon made Superintendent of the Wanshou Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang commended him at court; he was promoted to Direct Academician of the Baowen Pavilion and soon made Superintendent of the Wanshou Observatory.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shaoxing 7.

sentences.zh: 子砥，藝祖後令珦之子也。

translations.literal: Zidi was the son of Ling Bang, a descendant of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zidi was the son of Ling Bang, a descendant of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 仕至鴻臚丞。

translations.literal: He served up to the post of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 北遷至燕山，久之，欲遁歸，乃遣其徒朱國賓、王孝安至中京，求得上皇宸翰，懷之以歸。

translations.literal: Taken north to Yanshan, after a long time he wished to escape and return. He sent his followers Zhu Guobin and Wang Xiao'an to the Central Capital to obtain an autograph from the retired emperor, and brought it back concealed on his person.
translations.idiomatic: Carried north to Yanshan, he longed to escape. He sent Zhu Guobin and Wang Xiao'an to the Central Capital to obtain an autograph from the retired emperor and smuggled it back with them.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年六月，至行在，帝命輔臣召問于都堂。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Jianyan he reached the mobile court; the emperor ordered assisting ministers to summon him for questioning in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Jianyan 2 he reached the mobile court, and the emperor had his ministers question him in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 子砥言：「金人講和以用兵，我國斂兵以待和。

translations.literal: Zidi said: "The Jurchens use peace talks to prepare for war, while our state folds its arms waiting for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zidi said: "The Jurchens talk peace only to prepare for war, while we fold our arms waiting for peace.

sentences.zh: 往者契存丹主和議，女真主用兵，十餘年間竟滅契丹。

translations.literal: In the past the Khitan relied on peace talks while the Jurchens relied on arms; in little more than ten years they utterly destroyed the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Khitan trusted in treaties while the Jurchens trusted in arms; within a dozen years the Khitan were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 今復蹈其轍。

translations.literal: Now we are again treading in their footsteps.
translations.idiomatic: We are repeating their mistake.

sentences.zh: 譬人畏虎，啖虎以肉，食盡終必食人。

translations.literal: It is like a man who fears a tiger and feeds it meat; when the meat is gone, in the end it will eat the man.
translations.idiomatic: It is like feeding a tiger because you fear it: when the meat runs out, it will eat you.

sentences.zh: 若設陷阱待之，庶能制虎。」

translations.literal: If one sets traps and waits, one may perhaps control the tiger."
translations.idiomatic: Set traps instead, and you may yet master the tiger."

sentences.zh: 因復故官。

translations.literal: He was therefore restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 已而賜對稱旨，命知台州，卒。

translations.literal: Later, granted an audience, his answers pleased the emperor; he was appointed Prefect of Taizhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in a private audience, his answers pleased the emperor; he was appointed Prefect of Taizhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子晝字叔問，燕王五世孫。

translations.literal: Zizhou, courtesy name Shuwen, was a fifth-generation descendant of the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhou (Shuwen) was a fifth-generation descendant of the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 少警敏強記，工書翰。

translations.literal: As a youth he was alert, quick-witted, and had a strong memory; he was skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick-witted with an excellent memory and skilled in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 累官憲州通判。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Vice Prefect of Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Vice Prefect of Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，充詳定《九域圖志》編修官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanhe he served as revising compiler for the Detailed Verification of the Gazetteer of the Nine Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanhe he served as revising compiler for the Gazetteer of the Nine Circuits.

sentences.zh: 出知澤州，改密州。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Zezhou and was transferred to Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Prefect of Zezhou, then transferred to Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 詔爲刑部員外郎，以憂去。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, but left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice but left on account of mourning.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，遷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 4 he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尋用大宗正士㒟薦，遷尚書左司員外郎，兼權貨務，歲收茶、鹽、香錢六百九萬餘緡，以功進秩一階。

translations.literal: Soon, on the recommendation of Imperial Clan Scholar Shi, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Left Bureau of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Acting Superintendent of the Commodity Bureau; in a year he collected more than 6,900,000 strings from tea, salt, and incense, and for this merit was advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on Imperial Clan Scholar Shi's recommendation, he became Vice Director of the Left Bureau of the Department of State Affairs and Acting Superintendent of the Commodity Bureau; in one year he raised more than 6.9 million strings from tea, salt, and incense, and was promoted one rank for the achievement.

sentences.zh: 試太常少卿，集《太常因革禮》八十篇，爲二十七卷。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiled eighty chapters of the Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Reformed and Continued, in twenty-seven juan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiled eighty chapters of the Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Reformed and Continued, in twenty-seven scrolls.

sentences.zh: 上言復春分祀高禖禮。

translations.literal: He memorialized to restore the spring-equinox rite of sacrifice to Gaomei.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to restore the spring-equinox sacrifice to Gaomei.

sentences.zh: 除權禮部侍郎，遷徽猷待制、樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Rites, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Huixian Pavilion and Chief Secretariat Liaison of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Rites, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Huixian Pavilion and Chief Secretariat Liaison of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以公族爲侍從，及改官制後都承旨用文臣，皆自子晝始。

translations.literal: That an imperial clansman should serve as a palace attendant, and that after the reform of the bureaucracy the chief liaison post should employ a civil official—both began with Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first imperial clansman to serve as a palace attendant, and the first civil official appointed chief liaison after the bureaucratic reforms.

sentences.zh: 衢、嚴、信、饒之民，生子多不舉，子晝請禁絕之。

translations.literal: The people of Qu, Yan, Xin, and Rao commonly did not rear newborn sons; Zizhou petitioned to forbid and eliminate the practice.
translations.idiomatic: In Qu, Yan, Xin, and Rao, people commonly abandoned newborn children; Zizhou petitioned to ban the practice.

sentences.zh: 累求補外，遷徽猷閣直學士、知秀州。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sought an outside assignment, was transferred to Direct Gentleman of the Huixuan Pavilion and Prefect of Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sought a provincial post and was transferred to Direct Gentleman of the Huixuan Pavilion and Prefect of Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而奉祠以歸，寓于衢。

translations.literal: Later he received a temple sinecure and returned home, residing in Qu.
translations.idiomatic: He later took a temple sinecure and returned home, settling in Qu.

sentences.zh: 紹興十二年卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shaoxing he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shaoxing 12, aged fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 子潚字清卿，秦康惠王後，孝靖公令奧之子也。

translations.literal: Zisou, courtesy name Qingqing, was a descendant of Prince Kanghui of Qin and the son of Duke Xiaojing Ling Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Zisou, courtesy name Qingqing, was a descendant of Prince Kanghui of Qin and the son of Duke Xiaojing Ling Ao.

sentences.zh: 七歲而孤，家貧力學。

translations.literal: Orphaned at seven, his family was poor but he studied diligently.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at seven, he was poor but studied hard.

sentences.zh: 登宣和中進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the Xuanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination during the Xuanhe reign.

sentences.zh: 調真州刑曹掾，與守爭獄事，解官去。

translations.literal: Posted as an assistant in the criminal bureau of Zhen Prefecture, he quarreled with the prefect over a case, resigned his office, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned to the criminal bureau of Zhen Prefecture, he clashed with the prefect over a case, resigned, and left office.

sentences.zh: 改衢州推官。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as investigating clerk of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as investigating clerk of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 胡唐老奇其才，任之。

translations.literal: Hu Tanglao marveled at his talent and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tanglao admired his ability and entrusted him with responsibility.

sentences.zh: 屬時多故，子潚佐唐老繕完城具，苗、劉兵至城下，不能攻，以功進一秩。

translations.literal: As the times were troubled, Zisou assisted Tanglao in repairing the city defenses and equipment; when the armies of Miao and Liu reached the walls they could not take the city, and for this merit he was promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: In those troubled times Zisou helped Tanglao repair the city defenses; when the armies of Miao and Liu besieged the walls they could not breach them, and he was promoted one rank for the achievement.

sentences.zh: 累官吏部郎中，求補外，遷戶部郎中，總領江、淮軍馬錢糧。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, sought an outside assignment, was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and superintended funds and grain for military horses on the Yangzi and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, sought a provincial post, became Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and superintended funds and grain for military horses along the Yangzi and Huai.

sentences.zh: 諸司饋禮，月以千緡，悉歸之公帑。

translations.literal: Gifts from various offices totaled a thousand strings each month; he returned all of them to the public treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts from various offices came to a thousand strings a month; he sent all of them to the public treasury.

sentences.zh: 除直秘閣、兩浙轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant of the Secretariat Drafter and Vice Commissioner of the Liangzhe Transport Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant of the Secretariat Drafter and Vice Commissioner of the Liangzhe Transport Circuit.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣人檢沙田蘆場，欲概增租額，子潚以承買異冒占，力止之。

translations.literal: The court sent men to inspect sandy fields and reed flats, intending to raise rents across the board; Zisou argued that purchase contracts differed and titles were fraudulently occupied, and forcefully stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent inspectors to sandy fields and reed flats, intending a blanket rent increase; Zisou argued that purchase contracts varied and lands were falsely claimed, and he forcefully blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 時議者言：田之並太湖者被水患，宜分道諸浦注之江。

translations.literal: At the time debaters said that fields bordering Lake Tai suffered from floods and that channels should be opened to divert the water into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters at the time said fields bordering Lake Tai suffered flooding and that channels should be opened to drain the water into the river.

sentences.zh: 詔子潚往案視。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zisou to go inspect on site.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zisou to inspect the situation on site.

sentences.zh: 還言：「太湖當數州巨浸，豈松江一川所能獨泄。

translations.literal: On his return he reported: "Lake Tai is an immense basin spanning several prefectures—how could the Song River alone drain it?
translations.idiomatic: On returning he reported: "Lake Tai is a vast inland sea spanning several prefectures—how could the Song River alone carry it off?

sentences.zh: 昔人于常熟北開浦二十四以達大江，又開浦十于昆山東南以入海，今皆湮塞，宜加疏浚。」

translations.literal: In antiquity men opened twenty-four channels north of Changshu to reach the great river, and opened ten more channels southeast of Kunshan to reach the sea; today all are choked and should be dredged."
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times twenty-four channels were opened north of Changshu to reach the great river, and ten more southeast of Kunshan to reach the sea; all are now silted shut and should be dredged."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 遂浚常熟東柵至雉浦入于涇穀；

translations.literal: They then dredged from the east gate of Changshu to Zhipu, where it entered Jinggu.
translations.idiomatic: They dredged from the east gate of Changshu to Zhipu, where the water entered Jinggu.

sentences.zh: 又疏鑿福山塘，至尚市橋北注大江，分殺其勢，水患用息。

translations.literal: They also dredged Fushan Canal to Shangshi Bridge, where it flowed north into the great river, dispersing the force of the water, and flood woes ceased.
translations.idiomatic: They also dredged Fushan Canal to Shangshi Bridge, where it discharged north into the great river, breaking the force of the flood, and the water troubles subsided.

sentences.zh: 明州守趙善繼治郡殘酷，子潚率諸監司劾罷之。

translations.literal: The prefect of Ming Prefecture, Zhao Shanji, governed the commandery with cruelty; Zisou led the supervising commissioners to impeach and remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Prefecture's governor Zhao Shanji ruled with cruelty; Zisou led the circuit supervisors in impeaching and removing him.

sentences.zh: 除直敷文閣、知臨安府，吏不能欺，禁權家僦人子女爲僕妾者。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Attendant of the Fuwensge and Prefect of Lin'an; clerks could not deceive him, and he forbade powerful families from hiring people's sons and daughters as servants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Direct Attendant of the Fuwensge and Prefect of Lin'an, he left clerks no room to cheat and banned powerful families from hiring other people's children as servants and concubines.

sentences.zh: 詔權戶部侍郎，升敷文閣待制，復知臨安府。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Acting Vice Minister of Revenue and promoted him to Attendant Gentleman of the Fuwensge; he again served as Prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as Acting Vice Minister of Revenue, promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Fuwensge, and again made Prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 調三衙卒修築都城，不擾而辦。

translations.literal: He deployed soldiers of the Three Ya to repair the capital walls; the work was completed without disturbing the populace.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized soldiers of the Three Ya to repair the capital walls, finishing the work without troubling the people.

sentences.zh: 金主亮渝盟，子潚獻助軍一十五萬錢，特遷一秩。

translations.literal: When the Jurchen ruler Heli violated the treaty, Zisou contributed one hundred fifty thousand strings to aid the army and was specially promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchen ruler Heli broke the treaty, Zisou contributed one hundred fifty thousand strings to support the army and was specially promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 帝幸建康，充行宮留守參謀官。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Jiankang, he served as staff planning officer for the provisional palace garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Jiankang, he served as planning officer on the staff of the provisional palace garrison.

sentences.zh: 扈蹕還，復知臨安府。

translations.literal: He escorted the imperial procession on its return and again served as Prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted the imperial retinue home and again became Prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 金人來議和，子，子潚謂事情叵測，宜以軍禮待之。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens came to negotiate peace, Zisou said the situation was unpredictable and that they should be received with military protocol.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens came to negotiate peace, Zisou said the situation was unpredictable and that they should be received with military protocol.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，志圖恢復，子潚練兵，習爲「鵝鸛魚麗陣」，上觀于便殿，嘉之，賜金帶。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne with the aim of reconquest, Zisou drilled the troops and trained them in the "Goose-Crane Fish-Deer Formation"; the emperor watched in the side hall, praised him, and bestowed a golden belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong succeeded with plans for reconquest, Zisou drilled the troops in the Goose-Crane Fish-Deer Formation; the emperor watched from the side hall, praised him, and bestowed a golden belt.

sentences.zh: 擢敷文閣直學士，移知明州、沿海制置使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Gentleman of the Fuwensge and transferred to Prefect of Ming Prefecture and Coastal Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Gentleman of the Fuwensge and transferred to Prefect of Ming Prefecture and Coastal Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 台諫王十朋、王大寶抗疏留之，帝曰：「朕委以防海，行召還矣。」

translations.literal: Censors Wang Shipeng and Wang Dabao submitted forceful memorials to keep him; the emperor said: "I have entrusted him with coastal defense and will recall him soon."
translations.idiomatic: Censors Wang Shipeng and Wang Dabao submitted forceful memorials to keep him; the emperor said, "I have entrusted him with coastal defense and will recall him soon."

sentences.zh: 初，海寇以賂通郡胥吏，吏反爲之用，匿其蹤跡，賊遂大熾，商舶不通。

translations.literal: At first sea pirates bribed county clerks; the clerks in turn served them, hiding their tracks, so the bandits grew greatly in strength and merchant ships could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: At first sea pirates bribed county clerks, who then worked for them and concealed their movements; the pirates flourished and merchant shipping came to a halt.

sentences.zh: 子潚以禮延土豪，俾率郡胥分道入海，告之曰：「用命者有厚賞，不則殺無貸。」

translations.literal: Zisou courteously summoned local strongmen and had them lead county clerks by separate routes out to sea, telling them: "Those who obey will receive rich rewards; otherwise execution without mercy."
translations.idiomatic: Zisou courteously summoned local strongmen and had them lead county clerks by separate routes out to sea, telling them, "Obey and you will be richly rewarded; fail and you will be executed without mercy."

sentences.zh: 胥衆震恐，爭指賊處，悉禽獲。

translations.literal: The clerks were terrified and competed to point out where the bandits were; all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks were terrified and competed to point out the pirates' lairs; all were captured.

sentences.zh: 凡豪猾爲賊囊橐者，窮治之，海道遂平。

translations.literal: All powerful scoundrels who served as the bandits' financiers were thoroughly prosecuted, and the sea routes were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All powerful scoundrels who financed the pirates were thoroughly prosecuted, and the sea lanes were pacified.

sentences.zh: 陞龍圖閣直學士、知福州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Gentleman of the Longtu Pavilion and Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Gentleman of the Longtu Pavilion and made Prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，告糴旁郡，米價頓平，民賴以濟，進龍圖閣學士，移知泉州。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he petitioned to purchase grain from neighboring prefectures; grain prices promptly stabilized and the people were saved; he was advanced to Gentleman of the Longtu Pavilion and transferred to Prefect of Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine he petitioned to buy grain from neighboring prefectures; grain prices quickly stabilized and the people were saved; he was promoted to Gentleman of the Longtu Pavilion and transferred to Prefect of Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吏有掠民女爲妾者，其妻妒悍，殺而磔之，貯以缶，抵其兄興化掾，安廨中。

translations.literal: An official had seized a commoner's daughter as a concubine; his wife, jealous and fierce, killed and dismembered her, stored the remains in a jar, and sent it to his elder brother, a clerk in Xinghua, who kept it in his office.
translations.idiomatic: An official had seized a commoner's daughter as a concubine; his jealous, fierce wife killed and dismembered her, put the remains in a jar, and sent it to his elder brother, a clerk in Xinghua, who kept it in his office.

sentences.zh: 妾父每日郡訴，吏不決。

translations.literal: The concubine's father petitioned daily at the prefecture, but the official would not decide the case.
translations.idiomatic: The concubine's father petitioned at the prefecture every day, but the official would not decide the case.

sentences.zh: 子潚訪知狀，丞遣人往興化，果得缶以歸，獄遂決。

translations.literal: Zisou learned the facts on inquiry and sent an aide to Xinghua; the jar was indeed recovered and brought back, and the case was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zisou learned the facts on inquiry and sent an aide to Xinghua; the jar was recovered and the case was settled.

sentences.zh: 其發扌適概類此。

translations.literal: His exposures and investigations were generally of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His investigations were generally of this kind.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年卒于官，年六十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao he died in office, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in Qiandao 2, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 師𢍰

translations.literal: Shi Yu
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yu

sentences.zh: 師𢍰字從善，系出燕懿王。

translations.literal: Shi Yu, courtesy name Congshan, was descended from Prince Yiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yu, courtesy name Congshan, was descended from Prince Yiyan.

sentences.zh: 王生彰化軍節度使惟忠，惟忠生宣城侯從謹，從謹生崇國公世恬，世恬生嘉國公唆令。

translations.literal: The prince begat Weizhong, military commissioner of Zhanghua Circuit; Weizhong begat Congjin, Marquis of Xuancheng; Congjin begat Shitian, Duke of Chong; and Shitian begat Ling Jun, Duke of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: The prince begat Weizhong, military commissioner of Zhanghua Circuit; Weizhong begat Congjin, Marquis of Xuancheng; Congjin begat Shitian, Duke of Chong; and Shitian begat Ling Jun, Duke of Jia.

sentences.zh: 中興初，韓世清挾令唆爲變，裂黃旗被其身，固拒獲免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration, Han Shiqing coerced Ling Jun into rebellion, draped a yellow flag over his body, but he firmly refused and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Restoration, Han Shiqing coerced Ling Jun into rebellion, draped a yellow flag over him, but he firmly refused and was spared.

sentences.zh: 令唆生朝奉郎子笈，子笈生和州防禦使伯驌。

translations.literal: Ling Jun begat Ziji, Gentleman for Court Audience; Ziji begat Bozong, defender of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Jun begat Ziji, Gentleman for Court Audience; Ziji begat Bozong, defender of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 伯驌少从高宗于康邸，以文藝侍左右。

translations.literal: Bozong followed Gaozong from youth at the Kang residence and attended at his side by literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Bozong followed Gaozong from youth at the Kang residence and served at his side with literary talent.

sentences.zh: 師𢍰，伯驌之子也。

translations.literal: Shi Yu was the son of Bozong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yu was Bozong's son.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第，除司農簿，遷金部郎中。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed registrar in the Ministry of Revenue's agriculture bureau, and was transferred to Director in the gold bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed registrar in the Ministry of Revenue's agriculture bureau, and rose to Director in the gold bureau.

sentences.zh: 孝宗奇其才，顧遇頗厚。

translations.literal: Xiaozong marveled at his talent and favored him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong admired his talent and treated him with considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 師𢍰奏：左右曹、度支、倉部宜立總計，司歸併財物之數，以絕吏奸。

translations.literal: Shi Yu memorialized: the left and right bureaus, the expenditure bureau, and the granary bureau should establish a grand tally office to consolidate the numbers of goods and property, so as to cut off clerical fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yu memorialized that the left and right bureaus, the expenditure bureau, and the granary bureau should establish a grand tally office to consolidate goods and property and cut off clerical fraud.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 知吉州，即山煉銅，足冶欠額二十萬。

translations.literal: As Prefect of Ji Prefecture he smelted copper on the mountains and made up a shortfall of two hundred thousand in the smelting quota.
translations.idiomatic: As Prefect of Ji Prefecture he smelted copper on the mountains and made up a smelting shortfall of two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 進戶部郎官、淮東總領。

translations.literal: He was advanced to a director's post in the Ministry of Revenue and Superintendent of Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to a director's post in the Ministry of Revenue and made Superintendent of Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 光宗初，擢太府少卿、知秀州，改淮南運判。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangzong's reign he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and Prefect of Xiuzhou, then changed to Transport Judge of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangzong's reign he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and Prefect of Xiuzhou, then became Transport Judge of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 時郡鐵錢不行，鹽商弗至，師𢍰請發度牒，出倉粟，以收鐵錢，鹽利遂通。

translations.literal: At the time iron cash did not circulate in the prefecture and salt merchants did not come; Shi Yu requested the issuance of ordination certificates and the release of granary grain to collect iron cash, and the salt trade was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Iron cash did not circulate in the prefecture and salt merchants stayed away; Shi Yu requested ordination certificates and granary grain to collect iron cash, and the salt trade revived.

sentences.zh: 累遷司農卿、知臨安府。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Minister of Agriculture and Prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Agriculture and Prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 有僧號散聖者，以妖術惑衆，師𢍰捕治黥之。

translations.literal: There was a monk called San Sheng who deluded the masses with sorcery; Shi Yu arrested, punished, and tattooed him.
translations.idiomatic: A monk called San Sheng deluded the masses with sorcery; Shi Yu arrested him, had him punished, and tattooed.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄用事，師𢍰附之，遂得尹京。

translations.literal: When Han Tuozhou held power, Shi Yu attached himself to him and thereby became intendant of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou held power, Shi Yu attached himself to him and became intendant of the capital.

sentences.zh: 侂胄生日，百官爭貢珍異，師𢍰最後至，出小合曰：「願獻少果核侑觴。」

translations.literal: On Tuozhou's birthday the officials competed to present rare treasures; Shi Yu arrived last and produced a small box, saying: "I wish to offer a few fruit kernels to accompany the cup."
translations.idiomatic: On Tuozhou's birthday officials competed to present rare treasures; Shi Yu arrived last with a small box and said, "I wish to offer a few fruit kernels to accompany the cup."

sentences.zh: 啟之，乃粟金蒲萄小架，上綴大珠百餘，衆慚沮。

translations.literal: When it was opened, it proved to be a small stand of grapes wrought in gold, set with more than a hundred large pearls; the crowd was ashamed and discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: When it was opened, it held a small golden grape stand set with more than a hundred large pearls; the others were shamed into silence.

sentences.zh: 侂胄有愛妾十四人，或獻北珠冠四枚于侂胄，侂胄以遺四妾，其十人亦欲之，侂胄未有以應也。

translations.literal: Tuozhou had fourteen favorite concubines; someone presented him with four northern-pearl crowns, which he gave to four concubines; the other ten also wanted them, but Tuozhou had no way to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou had fourteen favorite concubines; someone gave him four northern-pearl crowns, which he gave to four of them; the other ten wanted crowns too, but Tuozhou had nothing to give them.

sentences.zh: 師𢍰聞之，亟出錢十萬緡市北珠，製十冠以獻。

translations.literal: When Shi Yu heard of this, he quickly spent one hundred thousand strings to buy northern pearls and made ten crowns to present.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Shi Yu quickly spent one hundred thousand strings to buy northern pearls and had ten crowns made as gifts.

sentences.zh: 妾爲求遷官，得轉工部侍郎。

translations.literal: A concubine asked that he be promoted, and he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A concubine asked that he be promoted, and he was made Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 侂胄嘗飲南園，過山莊，顧竹籬茅舍，謂師𢍰：「此真田舍間氣象，但欠犬吠雞鳴耳。」

translations.literal: Tuozhou once drank at the South Garden and, passing a mountain villa, looked at the bamboo fence and thatched hut and said to Shi Yu: "This is truly the air of a farmstead—only the barking of dogs and crowing of roosters are lacking."
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou once drank at the South Garden and, passing a mountain villa, looked at the bamboo fence and thatched hut and said to Shi Yu, "This is truly a farmstead scene—only barking dogs and crowing roosters are missing."

sentences.zh: 俄聞犬嗥從薄間，視之乃師𢍰也，侂胄大笑久之。

translations.literal: Soon a dog's howl was heard from the thicket; looking, they saw it was Shi Yu, and Tuozhou laughed long and hard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a dog's howl came from the thicket; looking, they saw it was Shi Yu, and Tuozhou laughed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 以工部尚書知臨安府。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Works and Prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Works and Prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 侂胄將用兵，師𢍰度侂胄材疏意廣，必召禍，乃持異論，侍御史鄭友龍劾罷之。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou was about to launch a military campaign, Shi Yu judged that Tuozhou's talent was shallow and his ambition broad, and that he would surely bring disaster; he therefore held dissenting views, and Supervising Censor Zheng Youlong impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuozhou was about to go to war, Shi Yu judged that his talent was shallow and his ambition overreaching and that he would bring disaster; he took dissenting views, and Supervising Censor Zheng Youlong impeached and removed him.

sentences.zh: 侂胄死，其黨多坐謫，以師𢍰嘗與侂胄異，故獲用。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou died, many of his faction were punished and banished; because Shi Yu had once differed from Tuozhou, he was retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuozhou died, many of his faction were punished and banished; because Shi Yu had once differed from Tuozhou, he was kept in office.

sentences.zh: 除寶謨閣直學士、知鎮江府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Gentleman of the Baomo Pavilion and Prefect of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Direct Gentleman of the Baomo Pavilion and Prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 會荊湖始置制閫，以命師𢍰，給事中蔡幼學繳其命，遂罷歸。

translations.literal: When Jinghu first established a military commissioner, Shi Yu was appointed; Supervising Secretary Cai Youxue rejected the appointment, and he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinghu first established a military commissioner, Shi Yu was appointed; Supervising Secretary Cai Youxue rejected the appointment, and he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔爲兵部尚書、知臨安府。

translations.literal: Before long an edict appointed him Minister of War and Prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was ordered to serve as Minister of War and Prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 幼學時爲學士，亦不草詔，留元剛草之。

translations.literal: Youxue was then an academician and likewise refused to draft the edict; Liu Yuangang drafted it instead.
translations.idiomatic: Youxue was then an academician and also refused to draft the edict; Liu Yuangang drafted it instead.

sentences.zh: 時楮輕糴貴，師𢍰尹京未數月，楮價浸昂，糴亦稍平，執政愈益賢之。

translations.literal: At the time paper notes were light and grain prices high; within a few months of Shi Yu's intendantcy in the capital, note prices gradually rose and grain prices eased somewhat, and the chief ministers increasingly regarded him as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Paper notes were weak and grain prices high; within a few months of Shi Yu's intendantcy in the capital, note prices rose and grain prices eased, and the chief ministers thought even more highly of him.

sentences.zh: 會武學士柯子沖、盧宣德以事至府，師𢍰擅撻遣之，衆盡讙，文武二學之士交投牒，師𢍰乃罷免，與祠。

translations.literal: When martial academy students Ke Zichong and Lu Xuande came to the prefectural office on business, Shi Yu arbitrarily had them flogged and sent away; the crowd rejoiced, students of both the martial and civil academies submitted petitions together, and Shi Yu was dismissed and given a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: When martial academy students Ke Zichong and Lu Xuande came to the prefectural office on business, Shi Yu had them flogged and sent away without authority; the crowd rejoiced, students of both academies submitted petitions, and Shi Yu was dismissed and given a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at home, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 師𢍰四尹臨安，有能聲。

translations.literal: Shi Yu served four times as intendant of Lin'an and had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yu served four times as intendant of Lin'an and had a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 嘗鉤致民罪，沒其家貲，謅事權貴，人以是鄙之。

translations.literal: He once entangled commoners in crimes, confiscated their family property, and fawned on the powerful; people despised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He once entangled commoners in crimes and confiscated their property, fawned on the powerful, and people despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 希言字若訥，惠王令懬元孫也。

translations.literal: Xiyan, courtesy name Ruone, was a grandson of Prince Hui Ling Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyan, courtesy name Ruone, was a grandson of Prince Hui Ling Kuan.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年登第。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chunxi he passed the examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination in Chunxi 14.

sentences.zh: 調衢州司戶，合郡民以計，表其坊，標其戶數，爲圖獻于守，守才之。

translations.literal: Posted as revenue clerk of Qu Prefecture, he counted the commandery's households by ward, labeled each ward, marked the number of households, and presented a map to the prefect, who admired his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned as revenue clerk of Qu Prefecture, he counted households by ward, labeled each ward with household totals, and presented a map to the prefect, who admired his ability.

sentences.zh: 西安令不職，守檄希言攝邑。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Xi'an was incompetent; the prefect ordered Xiyan to act as magistrate of the county.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Xi'an was incompetent; the prefect ordered Xiyan to act as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 漕善令，會嚴州請復烏龍嶺稅場，檄希言往訪之，俾令得復職。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner favored the magistrate; when Yan Prefecture requested restoration of the Wulong Ridge tax station, he dispatched Xiyan to investigate and allowed the magistrate to return to office.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner favored the magistrate; when Yan Prefecture requested restoration of the Wulong Ridge tax station, he sent Xiyan to investigate and let the magistrate return to office.

sentences.zh: 希言力陳烏龍場不當復，漕怒曰：「衢已復孔步、章戴二場，何烏龍獨不可復？」

translations.literal: Xiyan forcefully argued that the Wulong station should not be restored; the commissioner angrily said: "Qu has already restored the Kongbu and Zhangdai stations—why should Wulong alone not be restored?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiyan forcefully argued that the Wulong station should not be restored; the commissioner angrily said, "Qu has already restored the Kongbu and Zhangdai stations—why should Wulong alone not be restored?"

sentences.zh: 希言謂二場當並罷去，漕不能奪，二場竟亦廢。

translations.literal: Xiyan said both stations should be abolished together; the commissioner could not override him, and both stations were eventually abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyan said both stations should be abolished; the commissioner could not override him, and both were eventually shut down.

sentences.zh: 改吉州司理，屬邑有誣人以殺人罪者，吏治之急，囚誣服。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judicial clerk of Ji Prefecture; in a subordinate county a man was falsely accused of murder, the clerks pressed the case hard, and the prisoner falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to judicial clerk of Ji Prefecture, he found that in a subordinate county a man had been falsely accused of murder; clerks pressed the case hard and the prisoner falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 希言鞫得實，檄縣他捕，乃得真盜。

translations.literal: Xiyan interrogated and learned the truth, dispatched the county to arrest elsewhere, and thus obtained the real thief.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyan interrogated the case, learned the truth, and ordered the county to make arrests elsewhere; the real thief was caught.

sentences.zh: 用楊萬里、周必大薦，授臨安府司法，改淮西總所幹辦。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Yang Wanli and Zhou Bida he was appointed judicial officer of Lin'an Prefecture, then changed to staff officer of the Western Huai General Office.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Yang Wanli and Zhou Bida he was appointed judicial officer of Lin'an Prefecture, then became staff officer of the Western Huai General Office.

sentences.zh: 移書約諸郡：綱必時發，至即受納，無滯留。

translations.literal: He wrote to all prefectures stipulating: convoys must depart on schedule, and upon arrival grain must be received immediately, with no delay.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to all prefectures stipulating that convoys must depart on schedule and grain must be received immediately on arrival, with no delay.

sentences.zh: 始至，軍庫見錢不滿千緡，比去，庫錢充溢。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, visible cash in the army treasury was less than a thousand strings; by the time he left, the treasury was full.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, visible cash in the army treasury was less than a thousand strings; when he left, the treasury was full.

sentences.zh: 知臨安仁和縣。

translations.literal: He served as Prefect of Renhe County in Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Renhe County in Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 辟學宮四百餘畝。

translations.literal: He opened more than four hundred mu for the academy precinct.
translations.idiomatic: He opened more than four hundred mu for the academy precinct.

sentences.zh: 適大旱，蝗集御前蘆場中，互數里。

translations.literal: Just then a great drought struck, and locusts gathered in the imperial reed field, covering several li.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought locusts gathered in the imperial reed field, covering several li.

sentences.zh: 希言欲去蘆以除害，中使沮其策，希言驅卒燔之。

translations.literal: Xiyan wanted to remove the reeds to eliminate the pest; a palace eunuch obstructed the plan, but Xiyan drove his soldiers to burn them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyan wanted to clear the reeds to eliminate the pest; a palace eunuch blocked the plan, but Xiyan drove his soldiers to burn them.

sentences.zh: 臨平塘堤決，希言督役，親捧土投石，兵民爭奪，堤成，因築重堤，後不復決。

translations.literal: When the Linping pond embankment broke, Xiyan supervised the work, personally carrying earth and throwing stones; soldiers and civilians competed to join in; the embankment was completed, and a second embankment was built, after which it never broke again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Linping pond embankment broke, Xiyan supervised repairs, personally carrying earth and throwing stones; soldiers and civilians joined in; the embankment was rebuilt and a second one added, and it never broke again.

sentences.zh: 民病和買絹折錢重，希言節公費，代其輸。

translations.literal: The people suffered because the cash conversion for cooperative silk purchases was burdensome; Xiyan economized official expenses and paid on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The people suffered under heavy cash conversions for cooperative silk purchases; Xiyan cut official expenses and paid on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 除太社令，遷樞密院編修官兼右司。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Grand Sacrifice and transferred to Compiler in the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrently serving in the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Grand Sacrifice and transferred to Compiler in the Bureau of Military Affairs with concurrent duty in the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 上言：「諸將但務城守，敵來不拒，去不復追，異時之憂，殆不止保江而已。

translations.literal: He memorialized the throne: "The generals only concern themselves with holding the cities—when the enemy comes they do not resist, and when the enemy leaves they do not pursue. The troubles of later times will likely amount to more than merely holding the Yangtze line.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "The generals care only about holding the cities—they do not resist when the enemy comes, and they do not pursue when the enemy leaves. The troubles ahead will likely be worse than merely holding the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 宜諭諸將，一軍受圍，諸軍共守，敵不渡淮則均受賞，以戰爲守，毋以守爲守。」

translations.literal: Commanders should be instructed that when one army is besieged, all armies should defend together; if the enemy does not cross the Huai, all should share in the reward—take offense as defense, and do not treat defense as mere defense."
translations.idiomatic: He urged that commanders be told: when one army is besieged, all armies must defend together; if the enemy does not cross the Huai, all should share the reward—make fighting the means of defense, not defense an end in itself."

sentences.zh: 遷宗正丞，請南班得與輸對，許之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, requested that members of the southern branch be allowed to participate in imperial audiences, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, requested that southern-branch clansmen be allowed to attend imperial audiences, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書丞、著作郎、軍器少監，皆兼右司，又充密院檢詳，爲宰屬、樞掾凡六年，奉祠去。

translations.literal: He successively rose to Secretary, Compiler, and Assistant Director of the Arsenal Directorate, all while concurrently serving in the Right Bureau; he also served as Examiner in the Privy Council and as aide to the chief councilor and staff officer in the Bureau of Military Affairs for six years in all, then resigned to take a sacrificial stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Secretary, Compiler, and Assistant Director of the Arsenal Directorate, all while concurrently serving in the Right Bureau; he also served as Privy Council examiner and as chief-councilor aide and military-affairs staff officer for six years in all, then retired on a sacrificial stipend.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十七年卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died in the seventeenth year of Jiading, at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiading 17, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈資政殿大學士，封越國公，諡忠憲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance, enfeoffed as Duke of Yue, and given the posthumous name Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance, enfeoffed as Duke of Yue, and given the posthumous name Loyal and Disciplined.

sentences.zh: 子與權，登進士第，再中刑法科。

translations.literal: His son Yu Quan passed the jinshi examination and twice passed the penal law examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Quan passed the jinshi examination and twice passed the penal law examination.

sentences.zh: 官至開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He rose to Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the rank of Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 希懌字伯和，燕王八世孫。

translations.literal: Xiyi, courtesy name Bohe, was an eighth-generation descendant of the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi, courtesy name Bohe, was an eighth-generation descendant of the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 登淳熙十四年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Chunxi 14.

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚帥福建，希懌爲屬吏，嘗言：治人如修身，治政如理家，愛民如處昆弟。

translations.literal: When Zhao Ruyu was prefect of Fujian, Xiyi served as his subordinate official and once said: "Governing people is like cultivating the self; governing affairs is like managing a household; loving the people is like treating brothers."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ruyu was prefect of Fujian, Xiyi served on his staff and once said, "Governing people is like cultivating oneself; governing affairs is like running a household; loving the people is like treating one's own brothers."

sentences.zh: 取古今官著惠愛者緝爲一編，曰：「是吾師矣。」

translations.literal: He collected accounts of officials from ancient and modern times who were noted for benevolence and affection and compiled them into one volume, saying: "These are my teachers."
translations.idiomatic: He gathered accounts of officials from antiquity and his own day who were known for benevolent rule and compiled them into one volume, saying, "These are my teachers."

sentences.zh: 汝愚嘉之，薦于憲辛棄疾。

translations.literal: Ruyu admired this and recommended him to the intendant Xin Qiji.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu admired this and recommended him to the intendant Xin Qiji.

sentences.zh: 棄疾尚氣，僚吏不敢與可否，希懌獨盡言無所避。

translations.literal: Qiji was proud and imperious; the staff officials dared not disagree with him, but Xiyi alone spoke his full mind without holding back.
translations.idiomatic: Qiji was proud and overbearing; his staff dared not contradict him, but Xiyi alone spoke plainly without holding back.

sentences.zh: 屬邑候官苦稅重，每不登額，希懌稽核公帑羨錢以足之。

translations.literal: Subordinate counties suffered under heavy taxes and frequently failed to meet their quotas; Xiyi audited surplus funds in the public treasury to make up the shortfalls.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate counties groaned under heavy taxes and often failed to meet their quotas; Xiyi audited surplus public funds to cover the shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 棄疾亦薦其能。

translations.literal: Qiji also recommended him for his competence.
translations.idiomatic: Qiji also recommended him for his ability.

sentences.zh: 汝愚當國，調江東運司幹辦。

translations.literal: When Ruyu held power in the state, he was transferred to serve as coordinator in the Jiangdong Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruyu was chief councilor, Xiyi was transferred to serve as coordinator in the Jiangdong Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 同寅有坐侂胄党者，諸司莫敢薦，希懌賢其人，請以薦己者薦之。

translations.literal: A colleague had been implicated in the Han Tuozhou faction; no office dared recommend him, but Xiyi esteemed the man and asked that the person who had recommended himself be recommended in turn.
translations.idiomatic: A colleague had been implicated in Han Tuozhou's faction; no office dared recommend him, but Xiyi admired the man and asked to use his own recommendation slot for him.

sentences.zh: 改太平州通判。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as vice prefect of Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as vice prefect of Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是盜黥而逃者，捕得處死。

translations.literal: Previously, thieves who had been tattooed and fled were put to death when recaptured.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, tattooed thieves who fled were put to death when recaptured.

sentences.zh: 希懌言：「強盜特貸命而輒逃者斬，今黥罪致死，非法之平也。」

translations.literal: Xiyi said: "Robbers who are specially spared death but promptly flee are sentenced to decapitation; to put tattooed offenders to death now is not equitable under the law."
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi said, "Robbers who are specially spared death but then flee are decapitated; to put tattooed offenders to death now is not equitable under the law."

sentences.zh: 自是皆減死論。

translations.literal: From then on, all such cases were sentenced to reduced punishment short of death.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, all such cases received reduced sentences short of death.

sentences.zh: 遷江西茶鹽提舉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Intendant of Tea and Salt in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Intendant of Tea and Salt in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，惡少聚劫，希懌將自臨按，幕屬力止之，不聽，曰：「希懌不出，饑民終不得食，且召亂矣。」

translations.literal: In a year of famine, ruffians gathered to plunder; Xiyi was about to go in person to investigate, and his staff urgently tried to stop him, but he would not listen, saying: "If Xiyi does not go out, the famine-stricken people will never get food, and disorder will follow."
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year, ruffians gathered to plunder; Xiyi was about to go in person to investigate, and his staff urgently tried to stop him, but he would not listen, saying, "If I do not go out, the starving people will never get food, and disorder will follow."

sentences.zh: 遂行，發粟賑給，禽首謀者治之，其黨遂散。

translations.literal: He set out, distributed grain for relief, seized and punished the ringleaders, and their followers dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He set out, distributed grain for relief, seized and punished the ringleaders, and their followers dispersed.

sentences.zh: 升本路帥兼漕事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military commissioner of the circuit with concurrent charge of transport affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to circuit military commissioner with concurrent charge of transport affairs.

sentences.zh: 黑風峒羅世傳寇郴陽，奸民潛通賊，陰濟以糧。

translations.literal: Luo Shichuan of Black Wind Cave raided Chenyang; treacherous civilians secretly communicated with the bandits and covertly supplied them with grain.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shichuan of Black Wind Cave raided Chenyang; treacherous locals secretly communicated with the bandits and covertly supplied them with grain.

sentences.zh: 希懌捕治之，賊乏食，乃去。

translations.literal: Xiyi arrested and punished them; the bandits, lacking food, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi arrested and punished them; the bandits, short of food, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李元礪寇郴，陳廷佐寇南安，復誘羅世傳與合，劫掠至龍泉。

translations.literal: Before long, Li Yuanlei raided Chen; Chen Tingzuo raided Nan'an; they again induced Luo Shichuan to join with them, and together they plundered as far as Longquan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Li Yuanlei raided Chen, Chen Tingzuo raided Nan'an, and they again induced Luo Shichuan to join them; together they plundered as far as Longquan.

sentences.zh: 有何光世者，能知賊動息，希懌授光世計，俾誘世傳誅元礪以自贖。
