translations.literal: There was one He Guangshi who knew the movements of the bandits; Xiyi entrusted Guangshi with a plan to induce Shichuan to kill Yuanlei as a means of redeeming himself.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named He Guangshi who knew the bandits' movements; Xiyi entrusted him with a plan to induce Shichuan to kill Yuanlei and redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 功未竟，移知平江府，其後世傳果縛元礪以獻，廷佐勢孤，亦降。

translations.literal: Before the plan was completed, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture; afterward Shichuan indeed bound Yuanlei and presented him as a captive, and with his forces isolated, Tingzuo also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plan was completed, he was transferred to prefect of Pingjiang; afterward Shichuan indeed bound Yuanlei and presented him as a captive, and with his forces isolated, Tingzuo also surrendered.

sentences.zh: 移知太平州，希懌爲倅日，習知其民利病，遂損折帛價，減榷酤額，以蘇民力。

translations.literal: Transferred to serve as prefect of Taiping Prefecture, from his days as vice prefect Xiyi was well acquainted with the people's gains and grievances; he therefore reduced the price of tributary silk and cut the quota for the liquor monopoly to relieve the people's burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to prefect of Taiping, Xiyi already knew the people's hardships from his days as vice prefect; he reduced the price of tributary silk and cut the liquor-monopoly quota to relieve the people's burdens.

sentences.zh: 已而乞祠，遷端明殿學士，換昭信軍節度使、開府儀同三司，致仕。

translations.literal: He soon requested a sacrificial stipend, was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, exchanged posts to become military commissioner of the Zhaoxin Army and Acting Grand Preceptor, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested a sacrificial stipend, was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, exchanged posts for military commissioner of the Zhaoxin Army and Acting Grand Preceptor, and retired.

sentences.zh: 嘉定五年卒，年五十八，贈少保，封成國公。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Jiading at the age of fifty-eight; he was posthumously granted Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiading 5 at the age of fifty-eight; he was posthumously granted Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 士珸字公美，濮字懿王曾孫也。

translations.literal: Shigong, courtesy name Gongmei, was a great-grandson of Prince Yi of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Shigong, courtesy name Gongmei, was a great-grandson of Prince Yi of Pu.

sentences.zh: 天資警敏，兒時儼如成人。

translations.literal: He was naturally alert and quick; even as a child he carried himself like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: He was naturally sharp and quick; even as a child he carried himself like an adult.

sentences.zh: 比弱冠，爲右監門衛大將軍、貴州團練使。

translations.literal: By the time he reached adulthood, he was Grand General of the Right Gate Guard and Military Training Commissioner of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By adulthood he was Grand General of the Right Gate Guard and Military Training Commissioner of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從上皇北遷，次洺州東，與諸宗室議，欲遁還據城。

translations.literal: He accompanied the Retired Emperor on the northward relocation; when they halted east of Luo Prefecture, he conferred with other members of the imperial clan on a plan to slip away, return, and seize a city.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Retired Emperor on the northward relocation; when they halted east of Luo Prefecture, he conferred with other clansmen on slipping away, returning south, and holding a city.

sentences.zh: 謀未就而金人圍合，皆散走。

translations.literal: Before the plan could succeed, the Jurchens closed in on all sides, and all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plan could succeed, the Jurchens closed in from all sides, and everyone scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 士珸乘驢西亡，夜半盜奪驢去，徒步疾趨，遲明，抵武安酒家，語人曰：「我皇叔也。」

translations.literal: Shigong fled west on a donkey; at midnight a thief seized the donkey and ran off, and he hurried on foot; at daybreak he reached a wine shop in Wu'an and told people: "I am the emperor's uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Shigong fled west on a donkey; at midnight a thief seized the donkey and ran off, and he hurried on foot; at daybreak he reached a wine shop in Wu'an and told people, "I am the emperor's uncle."

sentences.zh: 邑官聞之來謁，資以衣冠鞍馬。

translations.literal: When the county officials heard this they came to pay their respects and supplied him with robes, a cap, a saddle, and a horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the county officials heard this they came to pay their respects and supplied him with robes, a cap, a saddle, and a horse.

sentences.zh: 因募得少壯百餘人，從至磁州，招集義兵以解洺圍。

translations.literal: He then recruited more than a hundred able-bodied men and proceeded to Ci Prefecture, where he gathered loyal militia to relieve the siege of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He then recruited more than a hundred able-bodied men and proceeded to Ci Prefecture, where he gathered loyal militia to relieve the siege of Luo.

sentences.zh: 旬日間，得勝兵五千人，歸附者數萬。

translations.literal: Within ten days he had five thousand seasoned troops, and tens of thousands came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he had five thousand seasoned troops, and tens of thousands came to join him.

sentences.zh: 時洺州守臣王麟欲叛降敵，軍民怒殺之，推統制韓一爲主。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Lin, the defending official of Luo Prefecture, wished to rebel and surrender to the enemy; the soldiers and people angrily killed him and elevated the commander Han Yi as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Lin, the defending official of Luo Prefecture, wished to rebel and surrender to the enemy; the soldiers and people angrily killed him and made the commander Han Yi their leader.

sentences.zh: 士珸夜半薄城下，力戰破圍。

translations.literal: Shigong reached the foot of the city wall at midnight and, fighting fiercely, broke through the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Shigong reached the foot of the city wall at midnight and, fighting fiercely, broke through the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 翌日入城，部分守禦。

translations.literal: The next day he entered the city and deployed the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he entered the city and deployed the defenses.

sentences.zh: 敵治壕塹，樹鹿角，示以持久。

translations.literal: The enemy dug moats and trenches, erected abatis, and showed their intention to prosecute a long siege.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy dug moats and trenches, erected abatis, and showed their intention to prosecute a long siege.

sentences.zh: 士珸礪將士死守，飛火炮碎其攻具，以計生得其首領，敵乃解圍去。

translations.literal: Shigong spurred his officers and men to hold firm; flying-fire cannons shattered their siege engines, and by stratagem he captured their leader alive; the enemy then lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shigong spurred his officers and men to hold firm; flying-fire cannons shattered their siege engines, and by stratagem he captured their leader alive; the enemy then lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以功遷權知洺州，仍兼防禦使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to acting prefect of Luo Prefecture, still concurrently serving as defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was transferred to acting prefect of Luo Prefecture, still concurrently serving as defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，金人再犯洺，糧盡援絕，衆不能守，乃擁士珸出城，由白家灘抵大名府，詔赴行在。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan the Jurchens attacked Luo again; grain was exhausted and relief cut off; the force could not hold; they then escorted Shigong out of the city, traveled by way of Baijia Beach to Daming Prefecture, and received an edict summoning him to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 2 the Jurchens attacked Luo again; grain was exhausted and relief cut off; the garrison could not hold; they escorted Shigong out of the city, traveled by way of Baijia Beach to Daming Prefecture, and received an edict summoning him to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，遷泉州觀察使，再遷平海軍承宣使、知南外宗正事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he was transferred to Observation Commissioner of Quan Prefecture, and later to Military Training Commissioner of the Pinghai Army and Director of the Southern Outer Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 5 he was transferred to Observation Commissioner of Quan Prefecture, and later to Military Training Commissioner of the Pinghai Army and Director of the Southern Outer Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 時泉邸新建，向學者少，士珸奏宗子善軫文藝卓絕，衆所推譽，乞免文解，由是人知激勸。

translations.literal: At that time the Quan residence had been newly built and few were inclined to study; Shigong memorialized that the clansman Shan Zhen was outstanding in letters and arts and widely praised, and requested exemption from the literary examination threshold—whereupon people came to know how to be stimulated and encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Quan residence had been newly built and few clansmen studied; Shigong memorialized that the clansman Shan Zhen was outstanding in letters and arts and widely praised, and requested exemption from the literary examination threshold—whereupon others were stirred to emulation.

sentences.zh: 遷節度使，未拜而卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner but died before he could assume the post, at the age of forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner but died before he could assume the post, at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈少師，追封和義郡王。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Heyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Heyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，諡忠靖。

translations.literal: During Chunxi he was given the posthumous name Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunxi he was given the posthumous name Loyal and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 子不流，歷臨安、紹興帥，治有聲。

translations.literal: His son Buliu served as prefect of Lin'an and Shaoxing in succession, and his governance won renown.
translations.idiomatic: His son Buliu served in succession as prefect of Lin'an and Shaoxing, and his governance won renown.

sentences.zh: 士㒟字立之，郇康孝王仲御第四子。

translations.literal: Shiyi, courtesy name Lizhi, was the fourth son of Prince Kangxiao of Xun, Zhongyu.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi, courtesy name Lizhi, was the fourth son of Prince Kangxiao of Xun, Zhongyu.

sentences.zh: 有大志，好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: He had great ambition, loved learning, and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He had great ambition, loved learning, and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 初補右班殿直，累遷忠州防禦使、鄭州觀察使，由寧遠軍承宣使轉權同知大宗正事。

translations.literal: He first entered service as Right Guard Attendant and successively rose to Defense Commissioner of Zhong Prefecture and Observation Commissioner of Zheng Prefecture; from Military Training Commissioner of the Ningyuan Army he was transferred to Acting Vice Director of the Great Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as Right Guard Attendant and successively rose to Defense Commissioner of Zhong Prefecture and Observation Commissioner of Zheng Prefecture; from Military Training Commissioner of the Ningyuan Army he was transferred to Acting Vice Director of the Great Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 時康王建大元帥府，士㒟請于孟太后，乞命帥府得承制便宜行事，又請奉王承大統，太后從之，王遂即位。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Kang was establishing a grand marshal's headquarters; Shiyi petitioned Empress Dowager Meng, requesting that the marshal's headquarters be granted imperial commission to act as circumstances required, and also requesting that the prince be installed to succeed the great line; the empress dowager consented, and the prince then ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Kang was establishing a grand marshal's headquarters; Shiyi petitioned Empress Dowager Meng, requesting that the headquarters be granted imperial commission to act as circumstances required, and also requesting that the prince be installed to succeed the throne; the empress dowager consented, and the prince then ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 除光山軍節度使，扈蹕南幸。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of the Guangshan Army and accompanied the imperial carriage on the southern journey.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of the Guangshan Army and accompanied the imperial carriage on the southern journey.

sentences.zh: 黃潛善等用事，士㒟論其誤國，潛善斥之，出知南外宗正事。

translations.literal: When Huang Qianshan and others held power, Shiyi criticized them for harming the state; Qianshan had him removed and sent him out to serve as Director of the Southern Outer Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Qianshan and others held power, Shiyi criticized them for harming the state; Qianshan had him removed and sent him out to serve as Director of the Southern Outer Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 會苗傅、劉正彥作亂，士㒟易服入杭，以蠟書遺張浚，趣其勤王；

translations.literal: When Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled, Shiyi changed his clothes, entered Hangzhou, and sent a wax-sealed letter to Zhang Jun urging him to march to rescue the throne;
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled, Shiyi changed his clothes, entered Hangzhou, and sent a wax-sealed letter to Zhang Jun urging him to march to rescue the throne;

sentences.zh: 復遺呂頤浩書，勉其與浚同濟國難。

translations.literal: he also sent a letter to Lü Yihao, urging him to join Jun in relieving the national crisis.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent a letter to Lü Yihao, urging him to join Jun in relieving the national crisis.

sentences.zh: 苗傅等怒浚，浚坐謫。

translations.literal: Miao Fu and the others were angered by Jun, and Jun was demoted as a result.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu and the others were angered by Jun, and Jun was demoted as a result.

sentences.zh: 復遺浚書，謂朝廷無他意，俾賊勿疑耳。

translations.literal: He again sent a letter to Jun, saying the court harbored no other intention, so that the rebels would not suspect otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent a letter to Jun, saying the court harbored no other intention, so that the rebels would not suspect otherwise.

sentences.zh: 事平，加檢校少保，除同知大宗正事。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was promoted to Honorary Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent and appointed Vice Director of the Great Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, he was promoted to Honorary Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent and appointed Vice Director of the Great Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復，除知大宗正事。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother, was recalled from mourning, and appointed Director of the Great Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother, was recalled from mourning, and appointed Director of the Great Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 請序位安定郡王下，從之。

translations.literal: He requested that his rank in precedence be placed below the Prince of Anding Commandery, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that his rank in precedence be placed below the Prince of Anding Commandery, and this was granted.

sentences.zh: 累乞祠，不許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested a sacrificial stipend but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly requested a sacrificial stipend but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 以定策功，詔其子不議改文秩，不怞易環衛官。

translations.literal: For his merit in settling the succession, an edict ordered that his sons Buyi be transferred to civil rank and Buyou exchanged for a palace guard commission.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in settling the succession, an edict ordered that his son Buyi be transferred to civil rank and his son Buyou exchanged for a palace guard commission.

sentences.zh: 加士㒟檢校少師。

translations.literal: Shiyi was promoted to Honorary Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi was promoted to Honorary Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 尋加開府儀同三司，判大宗正事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was further granted Acting Grand Preceptor and appointed Chief Judge of the Great Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was further granted Acting Grand Preceptor and appointed Chief Judge of the Great Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 入覲，勸帝留意恤民。

translations.literal: On entering audience, he urged the emperor to devote attention to caring for the people.
translations.idiomatic: On entering audience, he urged the emperor to devote attention to caring for the people.

sentences.zh: 金人既歸河南、陝西地，命士㒟謁陵寢，遂入柏城，披歷榛莽，隨宜葺治，禮畢而還。

translations.literal: After the Jurchens returned the territory of Henan and Shaanxi, he was ordered to pay reverence at the imperial tombs; he entered the cypress grove, cleared through the thicket, and repaired what needed repair as he went; when the rites were completed he returned.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jurchens returned the territory of Henan and Shaanxi, he was ordered to pay reverence at the imperial tombs; he entered the cypress grove, cleared through the thicket, and repaired what needed repair as he went; when the rites were completed he returned.

sentences.zh: 特封齊安郡王，以旌其勞。

translations.literal: He was specially enfeoffed as Prince of Qi'an Commandery to honor his service.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially enfeoffed as Prince of Qi'an Commandery to honor his service.

sentences.zh: 尋權主奉濮安懿王祠事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed acting custodian of the shrine to Prince Pu the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed acting custodian of the shrine to Prince Pu the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 軍興，罷宗室賜予，至有喪不能斂者，士㒟以聞。

translations.literal: With the outbreak of war, grants to the imperial clan were suspended, until some died and could not even be properly buried; Shiyi reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: With the outbreak of war, grants to the imperial clan were suspended, until some died and could not even be properly buried; Shiyi reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔緦麻、袒免親任環衛官而身亡者，賜錢有差。

translations.literal: An edict granted graded sums of money to those who had held palace guard posts among second- and fifth-degree mourners who died in office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted graded sums of money to clansmen in second- and fifth-degree mourning who had held palace guard posts and died in office.

sentences.zh: 長子不凡，方苗傅之亂，刲股納蠟書，持告張浚，以功轉兩官，易文資。

translations.literal: His eldest son Bufan, during the rebellion of Miao Fu, cut flesh from his thigh to conceal a wax-sealed letter inside and carried word to Zhang Jun; for this service he was promoted two ranks and exchanged for a civil commission.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Bufan, during the rebellion of Miao Fu, cut flesh from his thigh to conceal a wax-sealed letter inside and carried word to Zhang Jun; for this service he was promoted two ranks and exchanged for a civil commission.

sentences.zh: 從趙哲收復建州，殺葉濃，以功賜爵二級。

translations.literal: He followed Zhao Zhe in recovering Jian Prefecture and killing Ye Nong, and for this merit was granted two ranks of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhao Zhe in recovering Jian Prefecture and killing Ye Nong, and for this merit was granted two ranks of nobility.

sentences.zh: 士𡸕

translations.literal: Shichong
translations.idiomatic: Shichong

sentences.zh: 士𡸕字仰夫，太宗五世孫。

translations.literal: Shichong, courtesy name Yangfu, was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong, courtesy name Yangfu, was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 初以蔭補官，累轉太子率府副率。

translations.literal: He first entered office by yin privilege and successively rose to Vice Leader of the Crown Prince's Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered office by yin privilege and successively rose to Vice Leader of the Crown Prince's Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，隆祐太后幸洪州，敵奄至，百司散走。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan, Empress Dowager Longyou visited Hong Prefecture; the enemy suddenly arrived, and the hundred offices scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyan, Empress Dowager Longyou visited Hong Prefecture; the enemy suddenly arrived, and the hundred offices scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 士𡸕至一大船中，見二帝御容，負以走。

translations.literal: Shichong came to a large boat, saw portraits of the two emperors, and carried them away on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong came to a large boat, saw portraits of the two emperors, and carried them away on his back.

sentences.zh: 遇潰兵數百，同行至山中，衆欲聚爲盜，士𡸕出御容示之曰：「盜不過求食爲朝夕計耳，孰若仰給州縣。

translations.literal: He encountered several hundred routed soldiers; as they traveled together into the mountains, the crowd wished to gather as bandits; Shichong produced the imperial portraits and showed them to the men, saying: "Banditry is no more than scraping together food day by day—how is that better than relying on provision from the prefectures and counties?
translations.idiomatic: He encountered several hundred routed soldiers; as they traveled together into the mountains, the crowd wished to gather as bandits; Shichong produced the imperial portraits and showed them to the men, saying, "Banditry is no more than scraping together food day by day—how is that better than relying on provision from the prefectures and counties?

sentences.zh: 士𡸕以近屬諭之，必從。

translations.literal: As a close kinsman of the throne, Shichong would persuade them, and they would surely comply.
translations.idiomatic: As a close kinsman of the throne, Shichong would persuade them, and they would surely comply.

sentences.zh: 如此，則今日不饑餓，後日不失賞，是一舉而兩得也。」

translations.literal: In this way you would not go hungry today, and afterward you would not lose reward—one move and you gain both."
translations.idiomatic: In this way you would not go hungry today, and afterward you would not lose reward—one move and you gain both."

sentences.zh: 衆聽命。

translations.literal: The crowd obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd obeyed.

sentences.zh: 乃走謁太后虔州。

translations.literal: He then ran to pay homage to the empress dowager at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then ran to pay homage to the empress dowager at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 會虔民作亂，鄉兵在外爲應，與官軍相持。

translations.literal: Just then the people of Gan rebelled; militia outside the city responded to them and faced off against the government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the people of Gan rebelled; militia outside the city responded to them and faced off against the government troops.

sentences.zh: 士𡸕詣執政，謂當請太后急肆赦，人知免死，庶可安集；

translations.literal: Shichong went to the chief ministers and said the empress dowager should be asked to issue a general amnesty at once; once people knew they would be spared death, they could perhaps be settled;
translations.idiomatic: Shichong went to the chief ministers and said the empress dowager should be asked to issue a general amnesty at once; once people knew they would be spared death, they could perhaps be settled;

sentences.zh: 又宜急諭城中，城中定，則外寇可弭，譬如服藥，心腹已安，外禦風濕，乃餘事耳。

translations.literal: They should also urgently proclaim this within the city; once the city was settled, outside enemies could be quieted—like taking medicine: when the heart and belly are already at ease, guarding against wind and damp on the outside is a secondary matter.
translations.idiomatic: They should also urgently proclaim this within the city; once the city was settled, outside enemies could be quieted—like taking medicine: when the heart and belly are already at ease, guarding against wind and damp on the outside is a secondary matter.

sentences.zh: 赦既下，城中遂定。

translations.literal: Once the amnesty was issued, the city was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once the amnesty was issued, the city was settled.

sentences.zh: 遷右監門衛大將軍、惠州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand General of the Right Gate Guard and Defense Commissioner of Hui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand General of the Right Gate Guard and Defense Commissioner of Hui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十一年卒，贈建甯軍承宣使，追封建安郡王。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-first year of Shaoxing; he was posthumously granted Military Training Commissioner of the Jianning Army and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shaoxing 21; he was posthumously granted Military Training Commissioner of the Jianning Army and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jian'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 士皘，太宗之後，商、濮王之裔也。

translations.literal: Shigao was a descendant of Emperor Taizong and of the lines of the Princes of Shang and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Shigao was a descendant of Emperor Taizong and of the lines of the Princes of Shang and Pu.

sentences.zh: 從上皇俱北遷，乘間變姓名入僧寺中，落髮，衣僧衣以行，抵會稽。

translations.literal: He accompanied the Retired Emperor on the northward relocation; seizing an opportunity he changed his name, entered a Buddhist monastery, shaved his head, and traveled in monks' robes until he reached Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Retired Emperor on the northward relocation; seizing an opportunity he changed his name, entered a Buddhist monastery, shaved his head, and traveled in monks' robes until he reached Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 扈駕循幸，以覃恩轉千牛衛將軍奉朝請而卒。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial progress on the circuit tour; by grace of a general amnesty he was promoted to Colonel of the Thousand-Ox Guard with attendance at court, and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the imperial progress on the circuit tour; by grace of a general amnesty he was promoted to Colonel of the Thousand-Ox Guard with attendance at court, and then died.

sentences.zh: 不群字介然，太宗六世孫。

translations.literal: Buqun, courtesy name Jieran, was a sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Buqun (Jieran) was a sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，量試授承事郎。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe era, he passed the qualification examination and was appointed Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanhe era he passed the qualification examination and received appointment as Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，宰濟南章丘縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang, he served as magistrate of Zhangqiu County in Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Jingkang crisis he served as magistrate of Zhangqiu County in Jinan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 縣當山東、河北之沖，不群募效用五千人，增城浚濠，爲戰守備，敵攻圍兩月不能下。

translations.literal: The county stood at the crossroads of Shandong and Hebei; Buqun recruited five thousand volunteers-for-effect, heightened the walls and dredged the moat, and made preparations for offense and defense; the enemy attacked and besieged for two months without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay on the strategic corridor between Shandong and Hebei. Buqun recruited five thousand militiamen, raised the walls and dug out the moats, and prepared for both attack and defense; the enemy besieged the place for two months without breaking it.

sentences.zh: 遷維州通判，陞直秘閣，通判鎮江府，辟充兩浙宣撫司主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice prefect of Wei Prefecture, promoted to Direct Attendant of the Secret Archive, served as vice prefect of Runzhou Prefecture, and was recruited to serve as chief clerk for strategic planning in the Two-Zhejiang Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice prefect of Wei Prefecture, promoted to Direct Attendant of the Secret Archive, served as vice prefect of Zhenjiang, and was appointed chief clerk for strategic planning on the Two-Zhejiang Pacification Commission staff.

sentences.zh: 高宗在越，詔改郴州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong was at Yue, an edict reassigned him to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Gaozong was at Yue, an edict transferred him to Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時群盜出沒湖、湘間，不群嚴備禦，盜不能犯。

translations.literal: At the time bandits roamed back and forth between the lakes and Xiang region; Buqun maintained strict defenses, and the bandits could not penetrate them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were raiding across the lakes and Hunan region; Buqun tightened defenses until the robbers could no longer breach them.

sentences.zh: 進直顯謨閣，移知鼎州，充湖北兵馬副鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Hall for Exalted Planning, reassigned as prefect of Ding Prefecture, and appointed deputy military commander of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Hall for Exalted Planning, appointed prefect of Ding Prefecture, and made deputy military commander for Hubei.

sentences.zh: 既而朝廷慮郴失守，復留不群于郴。

translations.literal: Before long the court, fearing the loss of Chen, again retained Buqun at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon grew anxious that Chen might fall and kept Buqun there instead.

sentences.zh: 坐岳飛破曹成，成遁，因犯郴，不群乘城固守，拒卻之。

translations.literal: In connection with Yue Fei's defeat of Cao Cheng—Cheng fled and then struck at Chen—Buqun mounted the walls and held firm, beating them back.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue Fei routed Cao Cheng, Cheng fled and turned on Chen; Buqun mounted the walls and held firm, repelling the attack.

sentences.zh: 進直寶文閣，移知宣州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Hall of Treasured Culture and reassigned as prefect of Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Hall of Treasured Culture and appointed prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 軍需以時辦，而民不擾。

translations.literal: Military supplies were furnished on schedule, yet the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He met military needs on time without burdening the people.

sentences.zh: 進秩二階。

translations.literal: He advanced two ranks in grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 知廬州。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 酈瓊叛，擁不群北去，尋釋之以歸。

translations.literal: Li Qiong rebelled, seized Buqun and took him north; he was soon released and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qiong rebelled he carried Buqun off north with him, but Buqun was soon released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 帝召見，問瓊叛故，不群曰：「由劉錡除制置，瓊等以爲圖己，兼撫諭後時，故叛。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience and asked the reason for Qiong's rebellion; Buqun said: "It was because Liu Qi was appointed military commissioner; Qiong and the others thought the appointment was aimed at them, and moreover pacification orders came too late, so they rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and asked why Qiong had rebelled. Buqun said, "Liu Qi was appointed military commissioner; Qiong and his fellows believed the move was directed against them, and when pacification orders arrived too late, they rose in rebellion."

sentences.zh: 帝悔之。

translations.literal: The emperor regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to regret the decision.

sentences.zh: 除知荊南府，累遷兩浙路轉運副使，卒于官。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Jingnan Prefecture, was promoted in succession to vice transport commissioner of the Two-Zhejiang Circuit, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Jingnan, rose to vice transport commissioner of the Two-Zhejiang Circuit, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 不棄字德夫，太宗之裔。

translations.literal: Buqi, courtesy name Defu, was a descendant of Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Buqi (Defu) was a descendant of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，爲江東轉運判官。

translations.literal: During the Shaoxing era he served as transport vice commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing era he served as transport vice commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 秦檜忌四川宣撫使鄭剛中，以不棄能制之，除太府少卿、四川宣撫司總領官。

translations.literal: Qin Hui resented Sichuan Pacification Commissioner Zheng Gangzhong and, believing Buqi could check him, appointed Buqi Vice Director of the Palace Treasury and general supervisor of the Sichuan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui resented Sichuan Pacification Commissioner Zheng Gangzhong and, thinking Buqi could keep him in check, made him Vice Director of the Palace Treasury and general overseer of the Sichuan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 初，趙開總蜀賦，宣撫司文移率用申狀，不棄至官，用張憲成故事，以平牒見剛中。

translations.literal: Previously, when Zhao Kai supervised Shu taxation, the Pacification Commission generally used petition-style reports in its correspondence; when Buqi took office he followed the precedent of Zhang Xiancheng and presented himself to Gangzhong with a level memorandum.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Kai had overseen Shu taxation, the Pacification Commission routinely used petition-style documents; on taking office Buqi invoked the precedent of Zhang Xiancheng and addressed Gangzhong with a level memorandum—the form officials of equal rank used.

sentences.zh: 剛中愕然，久之始悟其不隸己，遂有隙。

translations.literal: Gangzhong was startled; only after some time did he realize Buqi was not subordinate to him, and enmity arose.
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong was taken aback and only gradually realized Buqi did not answer to him; from that point the two were at odds.

sentences.zh: 不棄欲盡取宣撫司所儲，剛中不與，不棄怒。

translations.literal: Buqi wished to take everything the Pacification Commission had stored; Gangzhong would not yield, and Buqi grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Buqi tried to seize everything held in the Pacification Commission stores; when Gangzhong refused, he flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 剛中辟利州轉運使王陟兼本司參議，不棄劾罷之。

translations.literal: Gangzhong recruited Lizhou Transport Commissioner Wang Zhi to serve concurrently as a deliberative officer on his staff; Buqi impeached him and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: Gangzhong recruited Wang Zhi, transport commissioner of Lizhou, as a concurrent staff deliberator; Buqi impeached Wang and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二人愈不相能，檜並召還，剛中在蜀，服用頗逾制，不棄復文致其事。

translations.literal: The two became ever less able to coexist; Qin summoned both back to court; while in Shu, Gangzhong's dress and furnishings largely exceeded regulations, and Buqi again memorialized to expose the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The two grew ever more hostile. Qin recalled both men. While still in Shu, Gangzhong's dress and household goods had largely exceeded what regulations allowed, and Buqi memorialized to expose him again.

sentences.zh: 檜乃罷剛中，升不棄敷文閣待制，知臨安府。

translations.literal: Qin then dismissed Gangzhong, promoted Buqi to Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Dispersed Literature, and appointed him prefect of Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qin dismissed Gangzhong, promoted Buqi to Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Dispersed Literature, and made him prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 逾年改工部侍郎，尋除敷文閣直學士、知紹興府。

translations.literal: After a year he was made Vice Minister of Works; soon afterward he was appointed Direct Academician of the Hall of Dispersed Literature and prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Vice Minister of Works, then Direct Academician of the Hall of Dispersed Literature and prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 時浙東旱，饑民多流亡。

translations.literal: At the time eastern Zhejiang suffered drought, and many starving people fled their homes.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhejiang was in drought and famine, and many people fled.

sentences.zh: 提舉秦昌時，檜兄子也，不棄言其悉心振恤，全活甚衆，昌時得遷秩。

translations.literal: Supervisory Commissioner Qin Changshi was Qin's nephew; Buqi reported that he had devoted himself wholeheartedly to relief, saving many lives, and Changshi received a promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory Commissioner Qin Changshi was Qin's nephew; Buqi reported that Changshi had devoted himself to relief and saved many lives, and Changshi was promoted.

sentences.zh: 其媚檜如此。

translations.literal: Such was the way he curried favor with Qin.
translations.idiomatic: This was how he courted Qin's favor.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 不尤，有武力。

translations.literal: Buyou possessed martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: Buyou was a man of martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 靖康之難，與王明募義兵，與金人戰，雄張河南、北。

translations.literal: During the calamity of Jingkang, he joined Wang Ming in recruiting righteous militia, fought the Jurchens, and made his power felt across north and south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang disaster he and Wang Ming raised righteous militia, fought the Jurchens, and made their names feared across the lands north and south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 盜皆避其鋒，曰：「此小使軍也。」

translations.literal: Bandits all avoided his edge and said: "This is the Little Commissioner-General."
translations.idiomatic: Bandits everywhere gave him a wide berth and said, "That is the Little Commissioner-General."

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，引衆歸，補武翼郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, he led his men back and was given a commission as Gentleman of Martial Valor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne, he brought his men in and was appointed Gentleman of Martial Valor.

sentences.zh: 從岳飛平湖寇。

translations.literal: He followed Yue Fei in pacifying lake bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Yue Fei in pacifying the lake pirates.

sentences.zh: 飛死，檜奪其兵，遣守橫州而卒。

translations.literal: When Yue Fei died, Qin seized his troops and sent Buyou to garrison Heng Prefecture, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue Fei was killed, Qin disbanded his command and sent Buyou to guard Heng Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 子善悉，進士登第。

translations.literal: His son Shansui passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shansui passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 累官敷文閣直學士、兩浙轉運副使。

translations.literal: He rose in office to Direct Academician of the Hall of Dispersed Literature and vice transport commissioner of the Two-Zhejiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Direct Academician of the Hall of Dispersed Literature and vice transport commissioner of the Two-Zhejiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯

translations.literal: Bushuai
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai

sentences.zh: 不𢙯字仁仲，嗣濮王宗暉曾孫也。

translations.literal: Bushuai, courtesy name Renzhong, was a great-grandson of Zong Hui, Prince of Pu of the succession line.
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai (Renzhong) was a great-grandson of Zong Hui, heir to the Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 父士圃，從上皇北遷，遙拜集慶軍節度使。

translations.literal: His father Shipu accompanied the Retired Emperor on the northward relocation and was appointed from afar as military commissioner of the Jiqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shipu accompanied the Retired Emperor north and was conferred from afar as military commissioner of the Jiqing Army.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯初補保義郎，紹興二十七年登第，易左宣義郎，調婺州金華丞。

translations.literal: Bushuai initially entered service as Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness; in the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing he passed the examination, exchanged for Left Gentleman for Expounding Righteousness, and was assigned as assistant magistrate of Jinhua in Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai entered service as Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness, passed the examinations in Shaoxing 27, exchanged his rank for Left Gentleman for Expounding Righteousness, and was posted as assistant magistrate of Jinhua in Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治縣豪河汝翼，械請于郡，編隸他州，邑人懾服。

translations.literal: He dealt with the county bully He Ruyi: fettered him and sent him up to the prefecture, registered him for service in another prefecture, and the townspeople submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He dealt with the county bully He Ruyi by shackling him and sending him to the prefectural seat, placing him on the register for service in another prefecture; the townspeople submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 除永州通判。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice prefect of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡歲輸米，倍收其贏，民病之，不𢙯言于守，損其數。

translations.literal: Each year when the prefecture submitted rice it collected double the surplus, to the people's distress; Bushuai spoke to the prefect and reduced the amount.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture each year doubled its collection of surpluses on rice tribute, burdening the people; Bushuai persuaded the prefect to reduce the levy.

sentences.zh: 帥司檄不𢙯錄靖州獄，辨出冤者數十百人，靖人德之，繪其像以祠。

translations.literal: The regional commander's office ordered Bushuai to review cases in the Jing Prefecture prison; he identified and freed scores of wrongfully accused persons, and the people of Jing were grateful to him and painted his portrait for worship.
translations.idiomatic: The commander's office ordered Bushuai to review Jingzhou prison cases; he cleared scores of wrongful convictions, and the people of Jing gratefully painted his portrait for worship.

sentences.zh: 除知開州。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Kai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 開在巴東，俗鄙陋，不𢙯爲興學，俾民知孝義。

translations.literal: Kai lay in Badong; the customs were coarse and backward; Bushuai established schools so the people would learn filial duty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Kaizhou lay in remote Badong, where manners were crude; Bushuai founded schools to teach the people filial piety and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 郡有鹽井，舊長吏必遣所親監之，私其處。

translations.literal: The prefecture had salt wells; former long-term officials invariably sent their own intimates to supervise them and kept the profits for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had salt wells, which long-term officials had habitually placed under the supervision of personal favorites so they could pocket the profits.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯罷遣，鹽利倍入，郡計用饒，以羨餘代民輸夏秋兩稅及天申節銀絹。

translations.literal: Bushuai abolished and dismissed these men; salt profits doubled, the prefecture's revenues grew ample, and with the surplus he paid the people's summer and autumn taxes and the silver and silk for the Heavenly Sovereign Festival.
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai dismissed those supervisors; salt revenues doubled, the treasury grew flush, and he used the surplus to pay the people's summer and autumn taxes and the silver and silk levy for the Heavenly Sovereign Festival.

sentences.zh: 在開二年，民絕鬥爭，夜戶不閉。

translations.literal: During his two years at Kai, the people wholly ceased fighting and did not shut their doors at night.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years the people had ceased brawling altogether and left their doors unbolted at night.

sentences.zh: 諸司交薦，以比古循吏。

translations.literal: Various agencies repeatedly recommended him, comparing him to the incorruptible officials of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Agencies throughout the bureaucracy recommended him as the equal of the model officials of old.

sentences.zh: 轉夔州轉運判官，開人數千遮城門，不得行。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport vice commissioner of Qizhou; several thousand people of Kai blocked the city gates so he could not depart.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to transport vice commissioner of Qizhou, thousands of Kaizhou residents blocked the city gates and would not let him leave.

sentences.zh: 至夔，民病上供銀。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Qizhou, he found the people burdened by the silver tribute for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Qizhou, he found the people crushed by the silver tribute owed to the court.

sentences.zh: 時部使者以親故攝大寧鹽場，專其利。

translations.literal: At the time a circuit commissioner had a relative acting as interim supervisor of the Daning salt works and monopolized the profits.
translations.idiomatic: A circuit commissioner had installed a kinsman as interim supervisor at the Daning salt works and kept the profits to himself.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯斥去，而鹽獲羨餘。

translations.literal: Bushuai drove him out, and the salt works produced a surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai removed him, and the salt revenues produced a surplus.

sentences.zh: 乃出錢市羨鹽數十萬斤，易米得三萬餘斛，運抵湖北，市銀以歸，代諸郡納上供銀，省緡錢十五余萬。

translations.literal: He then spent funds to purchase several hundred thousand catties of surplus salt, exchanged it for more than thirty thousand hu of rice, transported it to Hubei, sold it for silver and brought it back, paid the tribute silver on behalf of several prefectures, and saved more than one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He spent government funds to buy several hundred thousand catties of surplus salt, traded it for more than thirty thousand hu of rice, shipped the rice to Hubei, sold it for silver and brought the proceeds back, paid tribute silver on behalf of several prefectures, and saved more than one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 改成都路轉運判官。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as transport vice commissioner of the Chengdu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as transport vice commissioner of the Chengdu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 適歲饑，不𢙯行抵瀘南，貸官錢五萬緡，遣吏分糴。

translations.literal: It happened to be a famine year; Bushuai traveled to the southern border of Lu Prefecture, borrowed fifty thousand strings of official funds, and sent clerks out to purchase grain separately.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought famine; Bushuai went south to the Luzhou borderlands, borrowed fifty thousand strings from the treasury, and dispatched clerks to buy grain in several directions.

sentences.zh: 比至，下令曰：「米至矣。」

translations.literal: When they arrived he issued an order saying: "The rice has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: When the clerks arrived he proclaimed, "The rice has come."

sentences.zh: 富民爭發粟，米價遂平。

translations.literal: Wealthy households vied to release grain, and the price of rice quickly stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households rushed to release their grain, and rice prices quickly stabilized.

sentences.zh: 只流朱氏獨閉糴，邑民群聚發其廩。

translations.literal: Only the Zhu clan of Zhiliu alone hoarded grain and closed sales; townspeople gathered in a mob and broke open their granary.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Zhu clan of Zhiliu continued to hoard grain and refuse to sell; townspeople mobbed their granary and broke it open.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯抵朱氏法，籍其米，黥盜米者，民遂定。

translations.literal: Bushuai prosecuted the Zhu clan by law, registered their rice, tattooed those who had stolen grain, and the people were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai prosecuted the Zhu clan under the law, seized their grain, had the looters tattooed, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 永康軍歲治都江堰，籠石蛇絕江遏水，以灌數郡田。

translations.literal: Each year Yongkang Prefecture maintained the Dujiangyan irrigation works, caging stones into a coiled stone dam across the river to check the water and irrigate the fields of several prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Yongkang maintained the Dujiangyan works—stone-filled cages woven into a coiled dam across the river to hold back water and irrigate fields across several prefectures.

sentences.zh: 吏盜金，減役夫，堰不固而圮，田失水，故歲屢饑。

translations.literal: Clerks embezzled funds, reduced corvée laborers, the dam was not sound and collapsed, fields lost water, and therefore famine came year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Officials embezzled funds and cut the corvée crews; the dam failed and fields went dry, so famine returned year after year.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯躬視，操板築，繩吏以法。

translations.literal: Bushuai personally inspected the work, took up the tamping board himself, and punished the clerks according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai went in person to supervise, took up the tamping board himself, and punished the officials according to law.

sentences.zh: 乃出令：民業耕者田主貸之，事末作者富民振之，老幼疾患者官爲粥視。

translations.literal: He then issued an order: for the people whose livelihood was farming, landowners were to lend to them; for those in secondary occupations, wealthy households were to provide relief; for the old, the young, and the sick, the government was to provide gruel and care.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered that farmers receive loans from landowners, that those in trade be supported by wealthy households, and that the old, the young, and the sick be fed gruel at government expense.

sentences.zh: 全活數百萬。

translations.literal: He preserved the lives of several millions.
translations.idiomatic: Several million lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 黎州青羌奴兒結反，制司調兵往戍，屬不𢙯給餉。

translations.literal: Nu'erjie of the Qing Qiang in Lizhou rebelled; the Military Commission dispatched troops to garrison the area and assigned Bushuai to supply provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Nu'erjie of the Qing Qiang in Lizhou rebelled; the Military Commission deployed troops and put Bushuai in charge of provisions.

sentences.zh: 故事，富人出糧，而下戶以力致于邊。

translations.literal: By precedent, wealthy households supplied grain, while lower households contributed labor to transport it to the border.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, wealthy households furnished the grain while poorer households supplied the labor to haul it to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯曰：「民饑，不可擾也。」

translations.literal: Bushuai said: "The people are starving; they cannot be further disturbed."
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai said, "The people are starving—we cannot burden them further."

sentences.zh: 以糴余米發卒運之。

translations.literal: He used purchased surplus grain and sent soldiers to transport it.
translations.idiomatic: He used purchased surplus grain and sent soldiers to haul it.

sentences.zh: 已而朝廷命不𢙯攝製司。

translations.literal: Before long the court ordered Bushuai to serve as acting commissioner of the Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon appointed Bushuai acting commissioner of the Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 初，官兵敗，前制使遣人賂奴兒結以和。

translations.literal: At first, when government troops were defeated, the former commissioner sent men to bribe Nu'erjie to make peace.
translations.idiomatic: After an early defeat of government troops, the former commissioner had sent envoys to bribe Nu'erjie into peace.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯曰：「奴兒結，吐蕃小種也，今且和，若大族何？」

translations.literal: Bushuai said: "Nu'erjie is a petty branch of the Tibetans; if we make peace with him now, what of the great tribes?"
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai said, "Nu'erjie is only a minor Tibetan chieftain—if we make peace with him now, what will the major tribes demand?"

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 會酋豪夢束畜列率數千人入漢地二百餘里，成都大恐。

translations.literal: It happened that the chieftain Mengsu Chulie led several thousand men more than two hundred li into Han territory, and Chengdu was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftain Mengsu Chulie then led several thousand warriors more than two hundred li into Han territory, throwing Chengdu into panic.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯靜以鎮之，召僚屬飲。

translations.literal: Bushuai kept his composure to steady the people and summoned his subordinates to drink with him.
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai kept his composure to steady the city and invited his staff to dine with him.

sentences.zh: 夜遣步將領飛山軍徑赴沉黎，又徙綿州兵戍邛州爲後援，戒之曰：「堅守勿動。」

translations.literal: At night he sent infantry officers to lead the Feishan Army directly to Chenli, moved Mian Prefecture troops to garrison Qiong Prefecture as rear support, and warned them: "Hold firm and do not move."
translations.idiomatic: That night he sent infantry officers with the Feishan Army straight to Chenli, redeployed Mianzhou troops to guard Qiongzhou as a reserve, and ordered them, "Hold your positions—do not stir."

sentences.zh: 密檄諸蕃部：生獲吐蕃一人賞十縑，殺一人二縑。

translations.literal: He secretly issued orders to the various tribal departments: ten bolts of silk for capturing a Tibetan alive, two bolts for killing one.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly notified the tribal commands: ten bolts of silk for every Tibetan taken alive, two for every one killed.

sentences.zh: 于是邛部川首領崖襪合諸部落，大破吐蕃于漢源，斬夢束畜列首來獻，凡十有六日而平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Qiongbuchuan chieftain Yaimo united the various tribes, routed the Tibetans at Hanyuan, beheaded Mengsu Chulie and presented the head, and within sixteen days all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiongbuchuan chieftain Yaimo then rallied the tribes, crushed the Tibetans at Hanyuan, beheaded Mengsu Chulie and presented the head, and within sixteen days the crisis was over.

sentences.zh: 嘉州虛恨蠻入寇，不𢙯標吐蕃首境上，蠻懼，一夕遁去。

translations.literal: The Xuhuan barbarians of Jia Prefecture raided; Bushuai posted Tibetan heads on the border, the barbarians were afraid, and in one night they fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuhuan tribes of Jiazhou raided, Bushuai displayed Tibetan heads along the border; terrified, they fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯乃令緣邊家出丁夫一人，分戍諸堡，復其家。

translations.literal: Bushuai then ordered that each border household furnish one able-bodied man to garrison the forts in rotation, with tax relief for the household.
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai then required each border household to supply one man for rotating garrison duty at the forts, exempting the household in return.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯罷歸，蜀人送者自成都至雙流，遮道不得行。

translations.literal: When Bushuai was dismissed and returned, people of Shu who came to see him off from Chengdu to Shuangliu blocked the road so he could not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: When Bushuai left office, well-wishers from Chengdu to Shuangliu lined the road and would not let him pass.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除成都提刑，改江西路轉運判官。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed judicial intendant of Chengdu, then reassigned as transport vice commissioner of the Jiangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed judicial intendant of Chengdu, then transport vice commissioner of the Jiangxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 廷臣薦其賢，詔授右監門衛大將軍、惠州防禦使、知大宗正事。

translations.literal: Court officials recommended his worth; an edict appointed him Grand General of the Right Gate Guard, Defense Commissioner of Hui Prefecture, and Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials recommended him; by edict he was made Grand General of the Right Gate Guard, Defense Commissioner of Huizhou, and Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 非常制也。

translations.literal: This was not according to regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: This was an extraordinary appointment.

sentences.zh: 吏白承受奏請須用中貴人，不𢙯曰：「有司不存乎？」

translations.literal: A clerk reported that receiving memorials required the use of a palace eunuch; Bushuai said: "Do the regular offices no longer exist?"
translations.idiomatic: A clerk reported that imperial communications required a palace eunuch; Bushuai said, "Do the regular offices no longer exist?"

sentences.zh: 罷不用。

translations.literal: He abolished the practice and would not use them.
translations.idiomatic: He ended the practice and refused to use eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 中貴人或請見。

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs sometimes requested audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs sometimes asked for audiences.

sentences.zh: 輒謝出之。

translations.literal: He always declined and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He always refused and turned them away.

sentences.zh: 進明州觀察使，俄升昭慶軍承宣使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military training commissioner of Ming Prefecture and soon after elevated to military training commissioner of the Zhaoqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military training commissioner of Mingzhou and soon raised to military training commissioner of the Zhaoqing Army.

sentences.zh: 金人完顏烈來聘，充館伴副使。

translations.literal: When the Jurchen Wanyan Lie came on an embassy, he served as deputy host commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchen envoy Wanyan Lie arrived on a diplomatic mission, he served as deputy host commissioner.

sentences.zh: 金使從者舊見館使，皆對揖，不𢙯不爲禮。

translations.literal: Followers of Jin envoys who in former times had seen the host commissioner would all exchange mutual bows; Bushuai did not accord them such courtesies.
translations.idiomatic: Jin attendants who had met host commissioners before expected mutual bows; Bushuai refused to observe the custom.

sentences.zh: 宴玉津園，不𢙯連射皆中，使者驚服。

translations.literal: At a banquet in the Yujin Garden, Bushuai shot in succession and hit every target; the envoys were astonished and impressed.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in the Yujin Garden Bushuai hit every target in succession; the envoys were awestruck.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯以文行訓勉族屬，薦其秀傑者，奏新學宮，增廣弟子員，仿大學校定法。

translations.literal: Bushuai instructed and encouraged his kinsmen in literary conduct, recommended those who were outstanding, memorialized to build a new academy, expand the number of students, and follow the regulations of the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: Bushuai taught and exhorted his clansmen in learning and conduct, recommended the brightest among them, and memorialized to build a new academy, expand enrollment, and model its regulations on the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 置自訟齋，使有過者讀書其中，人人感勵。

translations.literal: He established a Hall for Self-Reproach, where those who had transgressed were made to study, and everyone was moved to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He established a Hall for Self-Reproach where offenders were set to reading, and every clansman was stirred to improve.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He died in the fourteenth year of Chunxi, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chunxi 14, at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，封崇國公。

translations.literal: Posthumously conferred Grand Master of the Mansion with the Privilege of Three Similitudes of Honor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the privilege of Three Similitudes of Honor as Grand Master of the Mansion and enfeoffed as Duke of Chong.

sentences.zh: 不𢙯性篤孝，生戒嚴歲，遭父北遷，每思慕涕泣。

translations.literal: Bushuai was deeply filial by nature. Born in the year of the Jieyan crisis, he suffered his father's forced removal to the north; whenever he thought of him he wept with longing.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, Bushuai was born in the year of the Jieyan disaster. When his father was taken north, the mere thought of him would bring him to tears.

sentences.zh: 長力學，母曹氏止之，答曰：「君父仇未報，非敢志富貴也。」

translations.literal: As he grew he devoted himself to study. His mother Lady Cao tried to stop him, and he replied: "The wrong done to my sovereign and father is unavenged—I dare not aspire to wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself to study as he grew older, but his mother Lady Cao tried to dissuade him. He replied, "The wrong done to my sovereign and father has not been avenged—I dare not set my heart on wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 登第時已入仕，法當超兩秩，請回授其母。

translations.literal: When he passed the examinations he had already entered office; by law he was due two extra ranks of promotion, and he asked that they be transferred back to confer upon his mother.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he passed the examinations he was already in office; the law entitled him to skip two ranks of promotion, but he asked that the honor be transferred to his mother instead.

sentences.zh: 母封法止令人，高宗嘉其志，特封郡夫人。

translations.literal: Regulations for conferring titles on mothers allowed only the rank of Lady; Gaozong admired his purpose and specially enfeoffed her as Lady of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rules for honoring mothers capped the title at Lady; the emperor admired Bushuai's devotion and made an exception, enfeoffing her as Lady of a Commandery.

sentences.zh: 居官所至有聲，立朝好言天下事。

translations.literal: Wherever he served in office he won repute; in court he liked to speak on affairs throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he earned a reputation for competence, and at court he was fond of speaking on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 蜀中武帥操重權，不𢙯請復置安撫司，相維而治。

translations.literal: In Shu the military commissioners wielded heavy power; Bushuai requested restoration of the Pacification Commission so the two offices might oversee each other in government.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu the military commissioners held overwhelming power; Bushuai petitioned to restore the Pacification Commission so the two offices could check and balance each other.

sentences.zh: 其論王抃不宜揀選諸路軍，王友直不可爲副都指揮使，尤人所難言者。

translations.literal: His arguments that Wang Bian should not select troops from the various circuits, and that Wang Youzhi should not serve as Vice Commissioner-in-Chief of the Capital Guard, were especially what others found hard to say.
translations.idiomatic: His objections—that Wang Bian should not be allowed to select troops from the various circuits, and that Wang Youzhi was unfit to serve as Vice Commissioner-in-Chief of the Capital Guard—were the sort of things others scarcely dared to say aloud.

sentences.zh: 遇大旱，一日九疏，勸上求直言，通下情，退而燔其稿。

translations.literal: During a great drought he submitted nine memorials in a single day, urging the emperor to seek blunt counsel and open channels to popular grievances; after retiring he burned the drafts.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought he submitted nine memorials in one day, urging the emperor to welcome blunt counsel and hear the people's grievances; afterward he burned the drafts.

sentences.zh: 時布衣上書狂悖，多抵罪，不𢙯謂太上皇帝不罪言者，此宜書之御座右。

translations.literal: At the time commoners who submitted wildly disrespectful memorials were often punished. Bushuai said the Retired Emperor's practice of not punishing those who spoke out should be written at the right hand of the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners who submitted wildly impertinent memorials were often punished; Bushuai argued that the Retired Emperor's policy of not punishing those who spoke out ought to be inscribed beside the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 帝悚然可之。

translations.literal: The emperor started in alarm and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled—and agreed.

sentences.zh: 既嘉其忠諒，每宴禁中，帝飲之酒，顧謂皇太子曰：「此賢宗室也。」

translations.literal: Having already commended his loyalty and forthrightness, whenever there was a banquet within the palace precincts the emperor would give him wine and, turning to the Crown Prince, say: "This is a worthy clansman.
translations.idiomatic: Having already praised his loyalty and candor, the emperor would at every palace banquet give him wine and, turning to the Crown Prince, say, "Here is a worthy member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 一日，坐待漏院，有給事中白英國公借擊球馬，不𢙯正色曰：「上惟一皇孫，萬一馬驚墮，斬汝輩無益也。」

translations.literal: One day, while sitting in the Dawn Waiting Courtyard, a Supervising Secretary reported that the Duke of Ying wished to borrow a polo horse. Bushuai said sternly: "His Majesty has but one imperial grandson—if the horse should startle and he fell, executing you lot would be of no use.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while waiting in the Dawn Waiting Courtyard, a Supervising Secretary reported that the Duke of Ying wished to borrow a polo horse. Bushuai said sternly, "His Majesty has only one imperial grandson—if the horse bolted and he fell, executing you would do no good.

sentences.zh: 馬竟不可得。

translations.literal: In the end the horse could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the horse was not lent.

sentences.zh: 所敬者朱熹、張栻，栻死爲請諡，又請用熹。

translations.literal: Those he honored were Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi. When Zhang Shi died he petitioned for a posthumous title, and he also petitioned to employ Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Those he most respected were Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi. When Zhang Shi died he petitioned for a posthumous title, and he also petitioned to put Zhu Xi to use in office.

sentences.zh: 其好尚如此。

translations.literal: Such were his preferences.
translations.idiomatic: Such were his tastes and convictions.

sentences.zh: 善俊字俊臣，太宗七世孫。

translations.literal: Shanjun, courtesy name Junchen, was a seventh-generation descendant of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Shanjun (Junchen) was a seventh-generation descendant of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 父不衰，閩路兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: His father Bu Shuai was Military Intendant of the Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bu Shuai served as Military Intendant of the Fujian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 善俊初補承節郎。

translations.literal: Shanjun initially entered service as Gentleman for Upholding Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Shanjun entered service as Gentleman for Upholding Integrity.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十七年登第。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing he passed the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations in Shaoxing 27.

sentences.zh: 換左承務郎，調南城丞，改昭信軍，簽判奇之。

translations.literal: He exchanged for Left Gentleman for Court Service, was assigned as assistant magistrate of Nancheng, transferred to Zhaoxin Army, and the judicial administrator thought him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged his rank for Left Gentleman for Court Service, was posted as assistant magistrate of Nancheng, then transferred to Zhaoxin Army, where the judicial administrator recognized his exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 虞允文亦薦其有邊帥才，除幹辦諸司審計司。

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen also recommended him as having the talent of a border commander, and he was appointed clerk in the Bureau for Auditing All Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen also recommended him as having the makings of a frontier commander, and he was appointed clerk in the Bureau for Auditing All Offices.

sentences.zh: 知郴州，敷奏稱旨，留爲太府寺丞。

translations.literal: As prefect of Chenzhou his memorials and reports pleased the throne; he was retained as Vice Director of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Chenzhou his memorials pleased the throne, and he was retained at court as Vice Director of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 尋攝帥、知廬州。

translations.literal: Soon he served concurrently as regional commander and prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served concurrently as regional commander and prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 會歲旱，江、浙饑，民麋至。

translations.literal: Famine struck alongside drought in the Jiang and Zhe regions, and refugees streamed in.
translations.idiomatic: Drought and famine afflicted Jiang and Zhe, and refugees poured in.

sentences.zh: 善俊括境內官田均給之，貸牛種，僦屋以居，死者爲給槥，人至如歸。

translations.literal: Shanjun seized state lands within the prefecture and distributed them evenly, loaned oxen and seed, rented dwellings for them to live in, and provided coffins for the dead; arrivals felt as though they had come home.
translations.idiomatic: Shanjun requisitioned state lands within the prefecture and distributed them evenly, loaned oxen and seed, rented houses for them to live in, and provided coffins for the dead; newcomers felt as if they had come home.

sentences.zh: 州城舊毀于兵，善俊葺完之，因言：「異時恃焦湖以通饋餫，今既堙涸，宜募鄉兵保孤、姥二山，治屋以儲粟。

translations.literal: The prefectural city had long lain in ruins from warfare. Shanjun rebuilt it, then said: "Formerly we relied on Jiao Lake to move provisions; now that it is silted dry, we should recruit local militia to hold Mount Gu and Mount Lao, and build storehouses to hoard grain.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural city had long lain in ruins from warfare; Shanjun rebuilt it and then said, "We once relied on Jiao Lake to move provisions, but now that it has silted dry we should recruit local militia to hold Mount Gu and Mount Lao and build storehouses to hoard grain.

sentences.zh: 敵或敗盟，則吾城守有餘，餉道無乏矣。」

translations.literal: If the enemy breaks the peace, our city will have sufficiency for defense and the supply routes will not fail.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy breaks the peace, our city will have enough to hold out and the supply routes will not fail.

sentences.zh: 又增築學舍，新包拯祠，春秋祀之，人感其化。

translations.literal: He also added school buildings and rebuilt the shrine to Bao Zheng, offering sacrifices in spring and autumn; the people were moved by his transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: He also expanded the school buildings and rebuilt the shrine to Bao Zheng, offering sacrifices in spring and autumn; the people were moved by his transforming influence.

sentences.zh: 累遷龍圖閣直學士，移知建州。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Academic Gentleman Directly Attached to the Hall of Dragon Designs and transferred as prefect of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Academic Gentleman Directly Attached to the Hall of Dragon Designs and was transferred as prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 建俗生子往往不舉，善俊痛繩之，給金穀，捐己奉，以助其費。

translations.literal: The custom in Jianzhou was often to abandon newborn children. Shanjun punished this severely, gave gold and grain, and contributed his own salary to help meet the costs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhou the custom was often to abandon newborn children; Shanjun punished this harshly, supplied gold and grain, and contributed his own salary to help families bear the cost.

sentences.zh: 再知廬州。

translations.literal: He served again as prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served again as prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 首言和好不可恃，當高城浚池以爲備。

translations.literal: He first memorialized that good relations could not be relied upon and that walls should be raised high and moats deepened as preparation.
translations.idiomatic: He first memorialized that peace with the enemy could not be trusted and that the walls should be raised and the moats deepened as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 復芍陂、七門堰，農政用修。

translations.literal: He restored Quepi and the Qimen Weir, and agricultural administration was put in order.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Quepi and the Qimen Weir, and agricultural administration was brought back into order.

sentences.zh: 免責屬邑坊場、河渡羨錢，百姓德之。

translations.literal: He remitted surplus levies from market booths and river ferries in subordinate counties; the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted surplus levies from market booths and river ferries in the subordinate counties, and the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去，服闋，起知鄂州。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his father's death; when mourning ended he was recalled as prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father; when the mourning period ended he was recalled as prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 適南市火，善俊亟往視事，弛竹木稅，發粟振民，開古溝，創火巷，以絕後患。

translations.literal: Just then fire broke out in the south market. Shanjun hastened to assume duties, waived the bamboo-and-timber tax, distributed grain to relieve the people, cleared ancient drainage channels, and opened fire lanes to prevent recurrence.
translations.idiomatic: Just then fire broke out in the south market; Shanjun hastened to take up his duties, waived the bamboo-and-timber tax, distributed grain to relieve the people, cleared old drainage channels, and opened fire lanes to prevent a recurrence.

sentences.zh: 僚屬爭言用度將不足，善俊曰「吾將瘠己肥人。」

translations.literal: Subordinates argued that expenditure would soon fall short. Shanjun said, "I intend to impoverish myself to enrich the people.
translations.idiomatic: His staff argued that funds would soon run short; Shanjun said, "I mean to make myself lean so the people may prosper.

sentences.zh: 乃省燕游車騎鼓吹之費，郡計用饒，代輸民役錢。

translations.literal: He reduced expenses for banquets, carriages, guards, and ceremonial music; the prefectural accounts grew ample, and he paid the people's corvée fees in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: He cut spending on banquets, carriages, escorts, and ceremonial music; the prefectural treasury grew ample, and he paid the people's corvée fees for them.

sentences.zh: 再知建州。

translations.literal: He served again as prefect of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served again as prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，民群趨富家發其廩，監司議調兵掩捕，善俊曰：「是趣亂也。」

translations.literal: In a year of famine the people rushed in crowds to rich households to break open their granaries. The supervisory commissioners discussed dispatching troops for a covert roundup. Shanjun said, "That would hasten chaos.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine the people rushed in crowds to wealthy households to break open their granaries; the supervisory commissioners proposed sending troops for a secret roundup. Shanjun said, "That would only hasten chaos.

sentences.zh: 諭許自新，平米價，民乃定。

translations.literal: He persuaded them, permitted self-renewal, stabilized grain prices, and the people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded them otherwise, allowed the offenders to reform, stabilized grain prices, and the people were calmed.

sentences.zh: 邑尉入盜十三人死罪，以希賞，善俊辨其冤。

translations.literal: The county captain entered thirteen men on capital charges for theft, hoping for reward; Shanjun established their innocence.
translations.idiomatic: The county captain had entered thirteen men on capital charges for theft, hoping for reward; Shanjun established their innocence.

sentences.zh: 徙知隆興府，移江西轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred as prefect of Longxing Fu and then moved to Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Transport circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred as prefect of Longxing Fu, then moved to Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Transport circuit.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷議減月樁錢，善俊言：「及州不及縣，則縣仍迫取于民，猶不減也。

translations.literal: At the time the court debated reducing the monthly pile levies. Shanjun said, "If the reduction reaches the prefecture but not the county, the counties will still press the people for collection—it will still not be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court debated reducing the monthly pile levies; Shanjun said, "If the cut stops at the prefecture and does not reach the counties, the counties will still press the people for payment—the burden will not truly fall.

sentences.zh: 宜一路通裁其額，下之漕臣，科郡縣輕重均減之。」

translations.literal: The quota should be cut uniformly throughout the circuit and sent down to the transport commissioner, who should distribute the reduction proportionally among prefectures and counties according to their burden.
translations.idiomatic: The quota should be cut uniformly across the circuit and sent down to the transport commissioner, who should distribute the reduction among prefectures and counties according to their respective burdens.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「和買已是白科，從而折變，益加糜費，其數反重于正絹，並乞蠲減。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Government procurement of silk is already an exaction levied in name only; to add conversion fees on top only wastes more, and the amount in the end exceeds the proper silk tribute—all this too should be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "Government procurement of silk is already an exaction in all but name; adding conversion fees on top only wastes more, and the total in the end exceeds the proper silk tribute—all of this should be remitted as well.

sentences.zh: 黥卒遇赦還者，刺充鋪兵，可除民害。」

translations.literal: Tattooed convicts who return after amnesty should be tattooed again and assigned as patrol soldiers—this would remove a menace to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooed convicts who return after amnesty should be tattooed again and assigned as patrol soldiers—this would remove a scourge upon the people.

sentences.zh: 所言多見用。

translations.literal: Much of what he proposed was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Much of what he proposed was adopted.

sentences.zh: 轉湖南帥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command Hunan.

sentences.zh: 郴、桂地絕遠，守多非才，善俊謂宜精其選。

translations.literal: Chen and Gui prefectures lay exceedingly remote, and their prefects were mostly without talent; Shanjun said the selection should be refined.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and Gui prefectures lay exceedingly remote, and their prefects were mostly men of little talent; Shanjun argued that the selection process should be tightened.

sentences.zh: 代輸潭州經、總制錢，停醴陵淥水渡錢。

translations.literal: He paid Tanzhou's circuit and overall-commission funds on the people's behalf, and abolished the Liling Lushui ferry toll.
translations.idiomatic: He paid Tanzhou's circuit and overall-commission funds on the people's behalf and abolished the Liling Lushui ferry toll.

sentences.zh: 加秘閣修撰，移知鎮江府。

translations.literal: He was given concurrent appointment as Compiler in the Secret Archive and transferred as prefect of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was given concurrent appointment as Compiler in the Secret Archive and transferred as prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，終喪而卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother and died when the mourning period ended, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 善俊風儀秀整，喜功名，尤好論事。

translations.literal: Shanjun's bearing was handsome and orderly; he delighted in merit and fame and especially loved to discuss public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shanjun's bearing was handsome and dignified; he delighted in merit and fame and especially loved to debate affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 孝宗時，日中有黑子，地屢震，每以飭邊備爲戒。

translations.literal: In Xiaozong's reign a black spot appeared in the sun and the earth shook repeatedly; he each time warned to tighten border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaozong's reign, when a black spot appeared in the sun and the earth shook repeatedly, he each time warned that border defenses must be tightened.

sentences.zh: 孝宗英武獨運，缺相者累年，善俊極言相位不可無人，尤人所難言者。

translations.literal: Xiaozong was heroic and martial and ruled alone; the post of chief councilor stood vacant for years. Shanjun spoke forcefully that the chief ministership must not go unfilled—again what others found hard to say.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was heroic and martial and ruled alone; the chief councilorship stood vacant for years. Shanjun spoke forcefully that the post must not remain empty—again, the sort of thing others scarcely dared to say.

sentences.zh: 善譽字靜之，父不倚，太宗之後也。

translations.literal: Shanyu, courtesy name Jingzhi; his father Bu Yi was also a descendant of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyu (Jingzhi) was the son of Bu Yi, himself a descendant of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 善譽幼敏慧，力學。

translations.literal: Shanyu was clever and quick from youth and devoted himself to study.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and quick from childhood, Shanyu devoted himself to study.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年，試禮部第一。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao he placed first in the Ministry of Rites examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 5 he placed first in the Ministry of Rites examination.

sentences.zh: 初調昌國簿，攝邑事。

translations.literal: His first appointment was as recorder of Changguo; he handled county affairs in an acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was as recorder of Changguo, where he handled county affairs in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 勸編戶裒金買田，以助嫁娶喪葬。
