translations.literal: He urged registered households to pool funds to buy fields to assist with marriages, burials, and funerals.
translations.idiomatic: He urged registered households to pool funds to buy fields to help one another with weddings, burials, and funerals.

sentences.zh: 捕得海盜全黨，守欲上其功，善譽曰：「奈何以人命希賞。」

translations.literal: When pirates were captured entire bands intact, the prefect wished to memorialize their merit. Shanyu said, "How can one hope for reward at the price of human lives?
translations.idiomatic: When an entire band of pirates was captured, the prefect wished to memorialize the achievement; Shanyu said, "How can one seek reward at the cost of human lives?

sentences.zh: 守益賢之，薦于朝。

translations.literal: The prefect admired him all the more and recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect admired him all the more and recommended him to the court.

sentences.zh: 授兩浙運幹，改知撫州臨川縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed clerk on the Two-Zhe transport staff and then changed to magistrate of Linchuan county in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed clerk on the Two-Zhe transport staff, then transferred to serve as magistrate of Linchuan county in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 縣嘗預借民賦，善譽閱籍發逋負，按籍征催，卒以時辦集，遂罷預借。

translations.literal: The county had formerly advanced taxes to the people; Shanyu examined the registers and discharged outstanding arrears, collected according to the register, and in the end all was delivered on time—so the advance practice was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The county had formerly advanced tax collections to the people; Shanyu examined the registers, cleared outstanding arrears, and collected according to the books until everything was delivered on time, after which the advance practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 改常州添差通判。

translations.literal: He was changed to supernumerary vice prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as supernumerary vice prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 史浩言其賢，詔赴部堂審察，累遷大理丞、湖北常平茶鹽提舉。

translations.literal: Shi Hao spoke of his worth, and an edict summoned him to the Ministry for evaluation; he rose in succession to Assistant Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review and Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries and the Tea-and-Salt Monopoly for Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hao spoke of his worth; an edict summoned him to the Ministry for evaluation, and he rose in succession to Assistant Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review and Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries and the Tea-and-Salt Monopoly for Hubei.

sentences.zh: 會大旱，善譽通融諸郡常平，計戶振貸，嗣歲麥禾倍收，民爭負以償。

translations.literal: During a great drought Shanyu pooled the ever-normal stores of the various prefectures, calculated households for relief loans, and the following year wheat and grain doubled in yield; the people vied to carry grain to repay.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought Shanyu pooled the ever-normal stores of the various prefectures and calculated relief loans by household; the following year wheat and grain yields doubled, and the people vied to carry grain to repay their debts.

sentences.zh: 奏罷稅場十餘、渡四十五，民便之。

translations.literal: He memorialized abolition of more than ten tax stations and forty-five ferries, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the abolition of more than ten tax stations and forty-five ferries, to the people's great relief.

sentences.zh: 俾諸郡售田，委郡文學董其入，以給計偕者。

translations.literal: He had the various prefectures sell fields and appointed county scholars to manage the income, to supply those traveling to the capital for the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He had the various prefectures sell fields and appointed county scholars to manage the proceeds, to support those traveling to the capital for the examinations.

sentences.zh: 移潼川路提刑、轉運判官。

translations.literal: He was moved to Judicial Intendant and Vice Commissioner of Transport for the Tongchuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Judicial Intendant and Vice Commissioner of Transport for the Tongchuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 遂甯守徐詡乏廉聲，部使者以其故御史，寬假之。

translations.literal: Xu Xu, prefect of Suining, lacked a reputation for integrity; the circuit envoy, because he had formerly been a censor, showed him leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xu, prefect of Suining, had no reputation for integrity; the circuit envoy, because Xu had formerly been a censor, showed him leniency.

sentences.zh: 善譽過遂寧，詡出迎，善譽抑使循廊，詡大沮。

translations.literal: When Shanyu passed through Suining, Xu came out to greet him; Shanyu forced him to walk the side corridor in submission. Xu was greatly humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanyu passed through Suining, Xu came out to greet him; Shanyu forced him to walk the side corridor in submission, and Xu was deeply humiliated.

sentences.zh: 郡人聞之，爭訟其過。

translations.literal: When the people of the prefecture heard of it, they competed to bring lawsuits against his misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of the prefecture heard of it, they rushed forward with lawsuits against his misconduct.

sentences.zh: 善譽劾諸朝，宰相王淮善詡，寢其章。

translations.literal: Shanyu submitted impeachments to the court, but Chief Councilor Wang Huai favored Xu and shelved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyu submitted impeachments to the court, but Chief Councilor Wang Huai favored Xu and shelved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 善譽徑以聞，罷詡。

translations.literal: Shanyu went directly to report to the emperor; Xu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyu reported directly to the emperor, and Xu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又以羨貲給諸郡置莊，民生子及娠者俱給米，威惠並孚。

translations.literal: He also used surplus funds to supply the various prefectures in establishing estates: rice was given alike to those who bore children or were pregnant, and both sternness and kindness won allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: He also used surplus funds to help the various prefectures establish relief estates, giving rice alike to women who gave birth and to those who were pregnant; both his sternness and his kindness won the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 宗子寓蜀者，少業儒，善譽即郡庠立學以教之，人始感勵。

translations.literal: Clansmen living in exile in Shu had seldom pursued Confucian study; Shanyu immediately established a school at the prefectural academy to instruct them, and people began to be stirred to effort.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen living in exile in Shu had seldom pursued Confucian learning; Shanyu immediately established a school at the prefectural academy to instruct them, and people began to be stirred to improve.

sentences.zh: 引年乞祠，歸處一室，以圖書自娛。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on grounds of age and a temple stipend, returned to live in a single room, and amused himself with books.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement on grounds of age and a temple stipend, returned to live in a single room, and amused himself with books.

sentences.zh: 無疾而卒，年四十七，時淳熙十六年也。

translations.literal: He died without illness, aged forty-seven, in the sixteenth year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died without illness at the age of forty-seven, in Chunxi 16.

sentences.zh: 善譽早失怙恃，撫育諸季備至，居官廉靖自將，多所著述，郭雍、朱熹嘗取其《易說》云。

translations.literal: Shanyu lost his parents early and raised his younger brothers with the utmost care. In office he maintained himself with integrity and restraint, wrote extensively, and Guo Yong and Zhu Xi drew upon his Commentary on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyu lost his parents early and raised his younger brothers with the utmost care. In office he maintained himself with integrity and restraint, wrote extensively, and Guo Yong and Zhu Xi drew upon his Commentary on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 汝述字明可，太宗八世孫。

translations.literal: Rushu, courtesy name Mingke, was an eighth-generation descendant of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Rushu (Mingke) was an eighth-generation descendant of Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖士說，從二帝北遷，臨河罵敵而死。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shishuo followed the Two Emperors north; facing the river he cursed the enemy and died.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shishuo followed the Two Emperors north; standing by the river he cursed the enemy and died.

sentences.zh: 汝述登淳熙十一年進士第。

translations.literal: Rushu passed the jinshi examinations in the eleventh year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: Rushu passed the jinshi examinations in Chunxi 11.

sentences.zh: 調南劍州順昌尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Shunchang in Nanjian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as magistrate of Shunchang in Nanjian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉定六年，詔主管官告院，自是常兼宰士，累遷將作少監，權侍立修注官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiading an edict appointed him director of the Office of Patent Letters; from then on he often concurrently served as palace attendant, rose in succession to Vice Director of Imperial Manufactories, and acted as record-keeper at imperial audiences.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading 6 an edict appointed him director of the Office of Patent Letters; from then on he often concurrently served as palace attendant, rose to Vice Director of Imperial Manufactories, and acted as record-keeper at imperial audiences.

sentences.zh: 八年，除起居郎兼密院都承旨，俄遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Gentleman of Attendance and concurrently Head Secretary of the Military Affairs Commission; soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Gentleman of Attendance and concurrently Head Secretary of the Military Affairs Commission; soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去，服闋，改邢部侍郎，遷尚書，知平江府，卒。

translations.literal: He left on account of his mother's death; when mourning ended he was changed to Vice Minister of Punishments, promoted to Minister, appointed prefect of Pingjiang Fu, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother; when the mourning period ended he was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments, promoted to Minister, appointed prefect of Pingjiang Fu, and died.

sentences.zh: 汝述爲尉，應詔上封事，論議懇惻。

translations.literal: When Rushu was a magistrate he responded to an edict with a sealed memorial; his arguments were earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: When Rushu was a magistrate he responded to an edict with a sealed memorial; his arguments were earnest and sincere.

sentences.zh: 立朝薦引，多知名之士。

translations.literal: At court he recommended and advanced many men of established reputation.
translations.idiomatic: At court he recommended and advanced many men of established reputation.

sentences.zh: 然爲時相所親，躐躋通顯，人亦以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet he was a favorite of the chief councilor of the time and leaped over ranks to prominent position; for this people thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was a favorite of the chief councilor of the day and leaped over ranks to prominence; for this people thought somewhat less of him.

sentences.zh: 叔近還秀州，已而王淵兵至杭，詐傳呼云：「趙秀州來。」

translations.literal: Shujin returned to Xiu Prefecture. Before long Wang Yuan's troops reached Hangzhou; they falsely cried out, "The Prefect of Xiu Zhao is here.
translations.idiomatic: Shujin returned to Xiu Prefecture. Before long Wang Yuan's troops reached Hangzhou, falsely crying out, "Prefect Zhao of Xiu is here.

sentences.zh: 通郊迎，淵遂誅之。

translations.literal: Shujin went out to the suburban greeting, and Yuan then executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shujin went out for the suburban greeting—and Yuan executed him.

sentences.zh: 初，淵在汴京，狎娼周氏，周氏後歸叔近，淵銜之，乃誣叔近通賊，奪職拘于州，以朱芾代之。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Yuan was in Bianjing he had consorted with the courtesan Lady Zhou; Lady Zhou later went to Shujin, and Yuan harbored resentment. He then falsely accused Shujin of communicating with bandits, stripped him of office and detained him in the prefecture, replacing him with Zhu Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Yuan was in Bianjing he had consorted with the courtesan Lady Zhou; Lady Zhou later became Shujin's, and Yuan nursed a grudge. He falsely accused Shujin of communicating with bandits, stripped him of office and detained him in the prefecture, and replaced him with Zhu Fu.

sentences.zh: 芾肆殘虐，軍民怨憤，小卒徐明率衆囚芾，迎叔近領郡事，叔近不得辭，因撫定之，請擇守于朝。

translations.literal: Fu was wantonly cruel; soldiers and civilians seethed with anger. The minor soldier Xu Ming led the crowd to imprison Fu and welcome Shujin to take charge of the prefecture. Shujin could not refuse; he therefore pacified and settled the affair and asked the court to choose a new prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was wantonly cruel, and soldiers and civilians seethed with anger. The minor soldier Xu Ming led the crowd to imprison Fu and welcome Shujin to take charge of the prefecture; Shujin could not refuse, pacified the situation, and asked the court to appoint a new prefect.

sentences.zh: 奏未達，朝廷命張俊致討。

translations.literal: Before the memorial arrived, the court ordered Zhang Jun to lead a punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial arrived, the court ordered Zhang Jun to lead a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 俊，淵部曲也，辭行，淵謂之「叔近在彼。」

translations.literal: Jun was Yuan's follower; he declined to go. Yuan told him, "Shujin is over there.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was Yuan's follower and declined to go; Yuan told him, "Shujin is over there.

sentences.zh: 俊諭意。

translations.literal: Jun understood the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jun understood what he meant.

sentences.zh: 領兵至郡，叔近出迎，俊叱令置對。

translations.literal: Leading troops to the prefecture, when Shujin came out to greet him Jun shouted an order to bring him before him for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: Leading troops to the prefecture, when Shujin came out to greet him Jun shouted an order to bring him in for questioning.

sentences.zh: 方操筆，群刀遽前，斷其右臂，叔近呼曰：「我宗室也。」

translations.literal: Just as he was taking up the brush, many swords suddenly advanced and severed his right arm. Shujin cried out, "I am of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he reached for the brush, blades rushed forward and cut off his right arm. Shujin shouted, "I am of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 俊曰：「汝既從賊，何云宗室！」

translations.literal: Jun said, "Since you followed bandits, how can you speak of being imperial clan!
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "You sided with rebels—how dare you claim to be of the imperial clan!

sentences.zh: 語未竟，已折首于地。

translations.literal: Before his words were finished, his head was already broken off upon the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could finish, his head was struck off to the ground.

sentences.zh: 徐明等見叔近死，遂反戈嬰城，縱火驅掠。

translations.literal: When Xu Ming and others saw Shujin dead, they turned their weapons about, held the city walls, set fires, and drove off plunder.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Ming and the others saw Shujin dead, they turned on their own side, barricaded the city, set fires, and looted the countryside.

sentences.zh: 翌日，俊斬關入，捕明等誅之。

translations.literal: The next day Jun broke through the gate and entered, captured Ming and the others, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jun forced the gate, entered the city, captured Ming and his followers, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 取周氏歸于淵，紹興九年，御史言叔近之冤，贈集英殿修撰。

translations.literal: He took Lady Zhou and sent her back to Yuan. In the ninth year of Shaoxing, a censor spoke of Shujin's wrongful death, and he was posthumously awarded Compiler of the Jiying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He took Lady Zhou and sent her back to Yuan. In Shaoxing 9 a censor spoke of Shujin's wrongful death, and he was posthumously granted the title Compiler of the Jiying Hall.

sentences.zh: 叔向，魏王之系也。

translations.literal: Shuxiang was of the line of the Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxiang belonged to the line of the Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 方汴京破時，叔向潛出，之京西。

translations.literal: When Bianjing fell, Shuxiang secretly escaped and went to the area west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Bianjing fell, Shuxiang slipped out in secret and made for the region west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 金人退，引衆屯青城，入至都堂，叱王時雍等速歸政，置救駕義兵。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens withdrew, he led his forces to camp at Qingcheng, entered as far as the chief council chamber, and shouted at Wang Shiyong and others to quickly restore the government, establishing righteous troops to rescue the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens withdrew, he led his men to camp at Qingcheng, marched into the chief council chamber, and berated Wang Shiyong and the others to restore the government at once, raising righteous troops to rescue the throne.

sentences.zh: 其後爲部將于渙上變，告叔向謀爲亂，詔劉光世捕誅之。

translations.literal: Later his subordinate general Yu Huan submitted a denunciation, reporting that Shuxiang plotted rebellion; an edict ordered Liu Guangshi to capture and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Later his subordinate general Yu Huan lodged a denunciation, accusing Shuxiang of plotting rebellion; an edict ordered Liu Guangshi to seize and execute him.

sentences.zh: 彥倓字安卿，彭城侯叔褧曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yantan, courtesy name Anqing, was a great-grandson of Marquis Pengcheng Shujiong.
translations.idiomatic: Yantan (Anqing) was a great-grandson of Marquis Pengcheng Shujiong.

sentences.zh: 父公廣，饒州太守。

translations.literal: His father Gongguang was prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gongguang had served as prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 彥倓初調溧陽尉，邑民潘氏兄弟橫邑中，號「三虎」，畜僮僕數百，邑官莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: Yantan's first assignment was as magistrate of Liyang; the Pan brothers among the county people tyrannized the county, called the "Three Tigers," kept several hundred servants, and no county official dared challenge them.
translations.idiomatic: Yantan's first posting was as magistrate of Liyang. The Pan brothers among the local people lorded over the county, styled the "Three Tigers," kept several hundred servants, and no county official dared stand up to them.

sentences.zh: 彥倓白其寧治之，縛潘氏弟，正其罪。

translations.literal: Yantan reported to the prefect and had them punished; he bound the younger Pan brother and settled his guilt according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Yantan reported the matter to the prefect and had the brothers punished; he bound the younger Pan brother and punished him according to law.

sentences.zh: 改揚州司戶，攝獄掾。

translations.literal: He was transferred to revenue clerk of Yangzhou and acted as prison assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to revenue clerk of Yangzhou and served concurrently as prison assistant.

sentences.zh: 有告主藏吏錢餘千萬，治之急，吏泣請死。

translations.literal: Someone reported that the chief storekeeper still had tens of millions in cash; when pressed in investigation, the clerk wept and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that the chief storekeeper still held tens of millions in cash; pressed hard in the investigation, the clerk wept and begged to die.

sentences.zh: 彥倓察其情，屏人問，則諸共貸也，攝宜興縣。

translations.literal: Yantan examined the circumstances; questioning him in private, he found it was all mutual loans among officials. He then acted as magistrate of Yixing county.
translations.idiomatic: Yantan looked into the matter and, questioning the clerk in private, found the money was all from mutual loans among officials. He was then assigned to act as magistrate of Yixing county.

sentences.zh: 縣自中興後，預借民明年稅，民挾此得慢其令。

translations.literal: Since the Restoration, the county had been advancing next year's taxes from the people; relying on this, the people grew disrespectful toward the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Restoration the county had been collecting the people's taxes for the following year in advance, and the people, holding this over the magistrate, treated him with contempt.

sentences.zh: 彥倓請禁預借，邑遂易治。

translations.literal: Yantan petitioned to forbid tax advances, and the county was then easily governed.
translations.idiomatic: Yantan petitioned to ban advance tax collection, and the county was soon easy to govern.

sentences.zh: 知臨安于潛縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yuqian county in Lin'an prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yuqian in Lin'an prefecture.

sentences.zh: 縣胥往往通台省吏，得肆其奸。

translations.literal: County clerks often colluded with clerks of the central ministries and provincial offices, enabling their malfeasance.
translations.idiomatic: County clerks often colluded with clerks of the central ministries and provincial offices, which let them run their schemes unchecked.

sentences.zh: 彥倓執其黠者，械送府。

translations.literal: Yantan seized the craftiest among them and sent them under restraint to the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Yantan seized the most cunning among them and sent them in fetters to the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 台省吏從中救之，彥倓力爭，竟抵胥罪。

translations.literal: Central and provincial clerks intervened to save them; Yantan struggled hard and in the end secured conviction of the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Central and provincial clerks intervened on their behalf, but Yantan fought the matter through and in the end secured the clerks' conviction.

sentences.zh: 浮橋屢以水敗，彥倓梁以石，民免溺死。

translations.literal: Floating bridges repeatedly failed from floodwater; Yantan bridged them with stone, and the people were spared drowning deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Floating bridges repeatedly washed out in floods; Yantan rebuilt them in stone, and the people were spared from drowning.

sentences.zh: 臨安府通判。

translations.literal: He became vice prefect of Lin'an prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of Lin'an prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開禧初，知興國軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaixi, he was appointed prefect of Xingguo Jun.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaixi era he was appointed prefect of Xingguo Jun.

sentences.zh: 歲旱蝗，而軍需急，屬邑令吳格負上供銀尤多，彥倓坐累貶秩格愧謝。

translations.literal: The year brought drought and locusts, while military supplies were urgent; Magistrate Wu Ge of a subordinate county was especially delinquent in tribute silver owed the court. Yantan was demoted in rank on account of the cumulative fault; Ge apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought drought and locusts while military needs were urgent; Magistrate Wu Ge of a subordinate county was especially behind in tribute silver owed the court. Yantan was demoted in rank on account of the accumulated shortfall, and Ge apologized in shame.

sentences.zh: 彥倓曰：「屬時多艱，宜寬民力以崇根本，何謝爲？」

translations.literal: Yantan said, "These are hard times—we should ease the people's burden to strengthen our foundations. What is there to apologize for?
translations.idiomatic: Yantan said, "These are hard times; we should ease the people's burden to strengthen our foundations. What is there to apologize for?

sentences.zh: 潰卒據外城爲變，彥倓募能斬捕者賞之。

translations.literal: Mutinous soldiers seized the outer city and rebelled; Yantan offered rewards to anyone who could capture or kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Mutinous soldiers seized the outer city and rose in revolt; Yantan offered rewards to anyone who could capture or kill them.

sentences.zh: 既而各斬首以獻，散其餘黨。

translations.literal: Before long each presented severed heads, and the remaining partisans were dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long severed heads were presented one after another, and the remaining rebels were dispersed.

sentences.zh: 累遷湖南運判。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to transport commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to transport commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 徭人羅孟傳反，累歲不能平。

translations.literal: The Yao tribesman Luo Mengchuan rebelled and for years could not be suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao tribesman Luo Mengchuan rebelled, and for years the uprising could not be put down.

sentences.zh: 彥倓謂帥臣曰：「徭人仇殺，乃其常情，況主斷不平，是遊之使叛也。

translations.literal: Yantan said to the commander, "Blood feud among the Yao is their ordinary custom; moreover, when verdicts are unfair, that is what drives wanderers to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Yantan said to the commander, "Blood feud is ordinary custom among the Yao; and when verdicts are unjust, that is what turns wanderers into rebels.

sentences.zh: 能遣諜者離其黨與，俾還自相仇，破之易矣。」

translations.literal: If we can send spies to split their factions and make them turn on one another, breaking them will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: If we send spies to split their factions and set them at one another's throats again, breaking them will be easy.

sentences.zh: 帥從其計，遂降隈傳。

translations.literal: The commander followed his plan, and Mengchuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The commander followed his plan, and Mengchuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 尋知紹興府。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Shaoxing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 楮價輕，彥倓權以法，民便之。

translations.literal: Paper currency had fallen in value; Yantan exercised authority according to law, and the people found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Paper currency had fallen in value; Yantan applied the law flexibly, and the people found this a relief.

sentences.zh: 復鹿鳴禮，置興賢莊以資其費。

translations.literal: He restored the Luming banquet ceremony and established an Xingxian Estate to fund its expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Luming banquet ceremony and established an Xingxian Estate to cover its costs.

sentences.zh: 築捍海石塘，亦置莊以備增築。

translations.literal: He built stone seawalls to repel the tide, also establishing an estate to prepare for future additions.
translations.idiomatic: He built stone seawalls against the tide and also established an estate to fund future repairs and extensions.

sentences.zh: 會，饑民聚陂湖中，彥倓取死囚，幕首刖足，徇于衆曰：「此劫蓤藕也。」

translations.literal: At one point hungry people gathered in the pond-lake areas; Yantan took condemned prisoners, covered their heads and cut off their feet, and displayed them to the crowd, saying, "These are those who robbed water caltrops and lotus roots.
translations.idiomatic: At one point hungry people gathered around the ponds and lakes; Yantan took condemned prisoners, hooded them and cut off their feet, and paraded them before the crowd, saying, "These men looted water caltrops and lotus roots.

sentences.zh: 遂散其衆。

translations.literal: The crowd was then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd then dispersed.

sentences.zh: 乃第民高下，損其稅有差，免輸湖籍田米，舉緡錢四十萬以助荒政，民賴以濟。

translations.literal: He then ranked the people by wealth, reduced their taxes by graduated amounts, exempted lake-field rice owed from registry holdings, and contributed four hundred thousand strings in cash to aid famine relief; the people were thus saved.
translations.idiomatic: He then ranked households by wealth, reduced taxes by graduated amounts, exempted rice owed from registered lake fields, and contributed four hundred thousand strings in cash to famine relief; the people were saved thereby.

sentences.zh: 詔改太府少卿，遷顯謨閣、知太平州，調江西轉運使。

translations.literal: An edict changed his post to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury; he was transferred to the Xianmo Pavilion and appointed prefect of Taiping prefecture, then reassigned as transport commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict transferred him to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury; he was promoted to the Xianmo Pavilion and appointed prefect of Taiping, then reassigned as transport commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十一年卒于官，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiading he died in office, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in Jiading 11, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 彥橚字文長，悼王七世孫。

translations.literal: Yansu, courtesy name Wenzhang, was a seventh-generation descendant of the Prince of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Yansu (Wenzhang) was a seventh-generation descendant of the Prince of Dao.

sentences.zh: 祖訓之在《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xunzhi is recorded in the "Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xunzhi is recorded in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 彥橚登乾道二年進士第。

translations.literal: Yansu passed the jinshi examinations in the second year of Qiandao.
translations.idiomatic: Yansu passed the jinshi examinations in Qiandao 2.

sentences.zh: 尉樂清，會大旱，令循故事禱雨，而責租益急。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Yueqing, during a great drought the prefect followed precedent to pray for rain but pressed rent collection all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Yueqing, during a great drought the prefect followed precedent in praying for rain while pressing rent collection all the harder.

sentences.zh: 彥橚曰：「損斂已責，所以和氣，何禱爲？」

translations.literal: Yansu said, "Cut levies that have already been demanded—that is how to restore harmonious qi. Why pray for rain?
translations.idiomatic: Yansu said, "Cut the levies already demanded—that is how to restore harmonious qi. Why bother praying for rain?

sentences.zh: 已而果雨。

translations.literal: Before long rain indeed fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long rain indeed fell.

sentences.zh: 累官福建路運幹，屬邑負振鹽本錢數千萬，累歲不能償，彥橚白其長，蠲之。

translations.literal: After rising to transport coordinator of the Fujian circuit, subordinate counties owed tens of millions in principal for disaster-relief salt funds and for years could not repay; Yansu reported to his superior and had the debt remitted.
translations.idiomatic: After rising to transport coordinator of the Fujian circuit, he found subordinate counties owed tens of millions in principal on disaster-relief salt funds and had been unable to repay for years; Yansu reported this to his superior and had the debt remitted.

sentences.zh: 慶元初，知晉陵縣，歲饑，彥橚振恤有方，所活幾二十萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingyuan, as magistrate of Jinling county, during famine Yansu organized relief effectively and saved nearly two hundred thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qingyuan era, as magistrate of Jinling county, during a famine Yansu organized relief effectively and saved nearly two hundred thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 又以羨錢爲五等戶代輸。

translations.literal: He also used surplus funds to pay taxes on behalf of households in the fifth tax grade.
translations.idiomatic: He also used surplus funds to pay taxes on behalf of fifth-grade households.

sentences.zh: 擢監登聞檢院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising censor of the Dengeen Investigation Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising censor of the Dengeen Investigation Office.

sentences.zh: 時韓侂胄方柄用，朝士悉趨其門，彥橚切歎惋。

translations.literal: At the time Han Tuozhou was in power; court officials all flocked to his door. Yansu deeply sighed in dismay.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Han Tuozhou held power, and court officials all flocked to his door; Yansu sighed deeply in dismay.

sentences.zh: 出知汀州，州民葉姓者，嘯聚汀、贛間，彥橚遣將捕戮之。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Tingzhou, there were people surnamed Ye among the prefecture's populace who gathered as bandits between Ting and Gan; Yansu dispatched generals to capture and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as prefect of Tingzhou, he found people surnamed Ye among the populace who had gathered as bandits between Ting and Gan; Yansu dispatched generals to capture and kill them.

sentences.zh: 遷廣西提刑，諸郡鬻官鹽，取息之六以奉漕司，系增至八分。

translations.literal: Promoted to judicial intendant of Guangxi: the various prefectures sold government salt and took six tenths of the interest to support the transport commission, which was progressively raised to eight tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to judicial intendant of Guangxi, he found that the various prefectures sold government salt and took six tenths of the interest for the transport commission, a share that had been progressively raised to eight tenths.

sentences.zh: 彥橚復其舊，以蘇民力，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: Yansu restored the original rate to relieve the people's burden; the court agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yansu restored the original rate to relieve the people's burden, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 侂胄死，詔戶部侍郎兼樞密院檢詳。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou died, an edict appointed him Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently Examining Officer of the Military Affairs Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuozhou died, an edict appointed him Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently Examining Officer of the Military Affairs Commission.

sentences.zh: 士大夫人前與兵議者，坐侂胄黨，將並逐之。

translations.literal: Scholars and officials who had earlier participated in military deliberations were implicated as partisans of Tuozhou and were about to be expelled together.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and officials who had earlier taken part in military deliberations were to be implicated as Tuozhou partisans and expelled together.

sentences.zh: 彥橚歎曰：「士方以偽學廢，今又以兵端斥去，苟欲錮士，何患無名！」

translations.literal: Yansu sighed and said, "Scholars have just been cast out for 'false learning,' and now they are to be driven off for having touched military matters. If one wishes to lock away scholars, what pretext will be lacking!
translations.idiomatic: Yansu sighed and said, "Scholars have just been cast out for 'false learning,' and now they are to be driven off for having touched military matters. If one wishes to shut scholars out of office, what pretext will ever be lacking!

sentences.zh: 每見帝，必言才難。

translations.literal: Each time he saw the emperor, he necessarily spoke of the scarcity of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw the emperor, he spoke of the scarcity of talent.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣總領。

translations.literal: He was transferred to overall director of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to overall director of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 舊士卒物故，大將不落其籍，而私其月請，彥橚置別籍稽核之。

translations.literal: Under the old practice when soldiers died, generals did not remove them from the rolls but pocketed their monthly stipends. Yansu established separate registers to audit this.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old practice, when soldiers died generals did not remove them from the rolls but pocketed their monthly pay. Yansu established separate registers to audit the rolls.

sentences.zh: 或傳軍中有怨言，彥橚曰：「不樂者主帥耳，何損士卒。」

translations.literal: It was rumored that there was discontent in the army. Yansu said, "Those who are displeased are the commanders—what harm does this do the soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: Rumor had it that the army was discontented. Yansu said, "It is the commanders who are displeased—what harm does this do the soldiers?

sentences.zh: 持之三年，掛虛籍者贏三萬，額減錢百萬緡，用度以饒。

translations.literal: After three years at this, phantom rolls exceeded thirty thousand names and nominal expenditures were reduced by a million strings; supplies became abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He persisted for three years; phantom rolls came to more than thirty thousand names, nominal expenditures were cut by a million strings, and supplies grew ample.

sentences.zh: 比去，餘七百萬，而諸路累積逋負猶四百萬，盡蠲之。

translations.literal: When he left, he still had seven million remaining, while accumulated arrears across the circuits amounted to four million—all were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office he still had seven million in surplus, while accumulated arrears across the circuits came to four million—all of which he remitted.

sentences.zh: 知平江府。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Pingjiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 郡之昆山並大海，盜出沒，可蹤跡，彥橚奏分其半置嘉定縣，屯兵以守。

translations.literal: The prefecture's Kunshan abutted the sea; pirates appeared and vanished traceably. Yansu memorialized to split off half the territory and establish Jiading county, garrisoning troops to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture's Kunshan bordered the sea, and pirates came and went along predictable routes. Yansu memorialized to split off half the territory and establish Jiading county, garrisoning troops to guard it.

sentences.zh: 轉寶謨閣待制。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Baomo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Baomo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 彥逾字德先，魏悼王後，崇簡國公叔寓曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yanyu, courtesy name Dexian, was descended from Prince Dao of Wei and was a great-grandson of Duke Chongjian Shuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyu (Dexian) was descended from Prince Dao of Wei and was a great-grandson of Duke Chongjian Shuyu.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十年登第。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations in the thirtieth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations in Shaoxing 30.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年，知秀州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunxi he was appointed prefect of Xiu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 5 he was appointed prefect of Xiu.

sentences.zh: 累遷太府少卿、四川總領。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and overall director of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and overall director of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 將入境，利西帥吳挺遣屬吏安丙來迓，彥逾見即喜其人，從容問之曰：「太尉統衆六萬，得無虛籍乎？」

translations.literal: Just before entering the border, the military commissioner of Li West, Wu Ting, sent his subordinate official An Bing to greet him. Yanyu was immediately pleased with the man and, speaking at leisure, asked him, "The Grand Marshal commands sixty thousand troops—surely there are no phantom rolls?
translations.idiomatic: Just before crossing the border, the military commissioner of Li West, Wu Ting, sent his subordinate An Bing to greet him. Yanyu took an immediate liking to the man and, speaking at ease, asked, "The Grand Marshal commands sixty thousand men—surely there are no phantom rolls on the books?

sentences.zh: 丙以情告。

translations.literal: Bing told him the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Bing told him the truth.

sentences.zh: 彥逾遺挺書，俾損虛籍數千，以寬四川之賦。

translations.literal: Yanyu sent Ting a letter instructing him to cut several thousand phantom rolls to lighten Sichuan's tax burden.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyu sent Ting a letter instructing him to cut several thousand phantom rolls and thereby lighten Sichuan's tax burden.

sentences.zh: 挺不敢隱。

translations.literal: Ting did not dare conceal the figures.
translations.idiomatic: Ting did not dare conceal the figures.

sentences.zh: 改知鎮江府，郡適旱饑，彥逾節浮費，發粟振糴，民賴以濟。

translations.literal: Transferred to prefect of Zhenjiang prefecture, the prefecture happened to suffer drought and famine. Yanyu cut unnecessary expenses, released grain for relief purchases, and the people were saved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to prefect of Zhenjiang, he found the prefecture in drought and famine. Yanyu cut unnecessary expenses, released grain for relief purchases, and the people were saved thereby.

sentences.zh: 會留正免相，汝愚登右揆，彥逾以端明殿學士出知建康，兼江東安撫使。

translations.literal: When Liu Zheng was dismissed as chief minister and Ruyu acceded to the right councilorship, Yanyu was sent out as Academic Fellow of the Duanming Hall to serve as prefect of Jiankang and concurrently military commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zheng was dismissed as chief minister and Ruyu rose to the right councilorship, Yanyu was sent out as Academic Fellow of the Duanming Hall to serve as prefect of Jiankang and concurrently military commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 未行，改撫制置使，兼知成都府。

translations.literal: Before he departed, he was changed to pacification and military commissioner, concurrently prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, he was reassigned as pacification and military commissioner, concurrently prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 彥逾爲政不擾，蜀人便安之。

translations.literal: Yanyu's governance was non-intrusive; the people of Shu found it comfortable and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyu's governance was unobtrusive, and the people of Shu found life under him comfortable and settled.

sentences.zh: 以定策勳，累遷資政殿大學士。

translations.literal: For merit in settling the succession, he was promoted in succession to Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in settling the succession, he was promoted in succession to Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰間，知明州兼沿海制置使。

translations.literal: During the Jiatai era he was prefect of Mingzhou and concurrently coastal military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiatai era he served as prefect of Mingzhou and concurrently coastal military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉定間，乞祠以歸，尋卒。

translations.literal: During the Jiading era he requested a temple stipend and returned home; he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiading era he requested a temple stipend and returned home; he soon died.

sentences.zh: 彥逾始與汝愚協濟大計，冀汝愚引己共政，及外除，頗觖望，乃疏當時名臣上之，目爲汝愚黨，帝由是疑汝愚。

translations.literal: Yanyu had at first joined Ruyu in the great enterprise of the succession, hoping Ruyu would bring him into shared governance; when he was sent out on provincial assignment, he was quite disappointed. He then drew up a list of eminent ministers of the day and submitted it, labeling them Ruyu partisans—by which the emperor came to suspect Ruyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyu had at first joined Ruyu in the great enterprise of settling the succession, hoping Ruyu would bring him into shared governance; when he was sent out on provincial assignment instead, he was deeply disappointed. He then drew up a list of eminent ministers of the day and submitted it, labeling them Ruyu partisans—and the emperor came to suspect Ruyu.

sentences.zh: 其兩入蜀皆有聲。

translations.literal: Both times he entered Shu he won a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Both times he entered Shu he won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 然吳氏世守武興，兼利西安撫，操重權。

translations.literal: However, the Wu clan had long held Wuxing and concurrently the Li West military commission, wielding heavy power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Wu clan had long held Wuxing while concurrently commanding the Li West military commission, wielding great power.

sentences.zh: 吳挺卒，朝廷用丘宗議，並利西安撫于東路，以革世將之弊。

translations.literal: When Wu Ting died, the court adopted Qiu Zongyi's proposal to merge the Li West commission with the Eastern Route, to reform the abuse of hereditary military appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Ting died, the court adopted Qiu Zongyi's proposal to merge the Li West commission with the Eastern Route, to reform the abuse of hereditary military command.

sentences.zh: 而彥逾奏利西安撫，乃領以武帥。

translations.literal: But Yanyu memorialized that the Li West commission should be held by a military commander.
translations.idiomatic: But Yanyu memorialized that the Li West commission ought to be held by a military commander.

sentences.zh: 其後吳曦因之以生變，人以是咎彥逾云。

translations.literal: Afterward Wu Xi exploited this to stir up rebellion; people for this reason blamed Yanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Wu Xi exploited this arrangement to stir up rebellion, and people blamed Yanyu for it.
